delete.summary:
Drops an Iceberg table and removes every trace of it the console owns:
the Trino table itself, the declarative `TrinoTable` CRD (when the table
was declared rather than ad-hoc) and the DB metadata row.
delete.description:
Addressed by `(schema_name, table_name)` rather than a UUID because the
list endpoint synthesizes rows for CRD-declared tables that have no DB
row yet — those carry a nil id and would be undeletable by id.

The `DROP TABLE` runs first, as the user, so Trino/OPA enforce the
caller's own privileges and a permission failure aborts before anything
is unwound. The CRD is force-removed afterwards: its finalizer only
drops the table when `reclaimPolicy: Delete`, and the table is already
gone by then either way.

That ordering is deliberate but not atomic: if the CRD removal fails
after the DROP succeeded, the declaration outlives the table and the
operator's drift reconciler recreates it *empty* within one
`DRIFT_CHECK_INTERVAL`. The error message says so, because the user has
to delete the `TrinoTable` object to make it stick. The reverse order
would be worse: a caller whom OPA then refuses would have stripped the
declaration off a table that is still standing, turning a governed table
into an unmanaged one without ever holding the privilege to drop it.

post.description:
This is the "generate a scoped key" flow: rather than the caller bringing a
service account, the console creates a dedicated, customer-owned one carrying
exactly the requested grants and mints the key for it. The account is a normal
service account — visible in IAM, deletable by the customer — so revoking the
key is either revoking it or deleting the account. The grants are unanchored
(not platform-owned), so the customer keeps full control of them.

The route resolves exactly ONE gateway target (one zone, hence one Ceph
`target.tenant`) for the whole request, so every bucket in `scopes` is
granted under that same tenant. This is correct only because all requested
buckets belong to that one resolved zone — the frontend must only ever offer
same-zone buckets in the picker. See [`scoped_bucket_paths`].

If anything after the account is created fails, the account is torn down
best-effort so a half-provisioned identity is not left behind.

patch.description:
`true` makes every harbor created *after* the flip receive a dedicated
`hf-{org}-{harbor}` Kubernetes namespace, stamped once at harbor INSERT;
existing harbors are untouched (migrating them is separate, out-of-scope
tooling). `false` restores/keeps legacy shared `hf-{org}` placement for

state where the flag says "shared" but a harbor's workloads are already
placed in their own namespace. The guard holds a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the

takes that same lock, so a concurrent create cannot slip a stamp past it.

only at INSERT and no API ever back-fills it, an org that opted in and
created one dedicated harbor can only opt back out by deleting that harbor
(see ADR-0031, "Known operational constraints").

settings"), the same permission any org-settings mutation requires, plus
the org member guard — mirroring the logs-retention route's scope.

post.description:
## The credential is proved against GitHub before it is stored
A credential is only worth storing if GitHub accepts it, and the cost of
finding out later is high: an unusable credential is accepted silently
today, and the first symptom is a pool that never comes online, with the
real reason buried in an ARC listener log the user cannot see. So the
connection is used, once, before anything is written — and if GitHub
refuses it, the 400 carries GitHub's own sentence ("Bad credentials",
"Integration not found", …).

The same round trip is what makes `installation_id` optional for the App
case: `GET /app/installations` answers it. See [`resolve_app_installation`].

put.description:
## Why the credential is always required
The stored credential is write-only — no endpoint hands one back — so there
is nothing here to partially edit. Requiring it also means every update
re-proves a working credential against the *effective* host before anything
is overwritten, which is what makes the failure mode "GitHub refused this,
nothing changed" instead of "your pools stop renewing their registration
token an hour from now".

The name is not editable: it is what every pool's `connection_secret_name`
resolves through, and renaming it would orphan them. Rename = create the new
one, move the pools, delete the old one.

## Propagation
The operator re-projects each pool's `githubConfigSecret` from this secret
on every reconcile, so a rotation reaches running pools on their next tick
(~2 minutes for a healthy pool) with no pool edit and no restart.

The forge coordinates are resolved automatically from `harbor_id` —
the caller never supplies `forge_namespace` or `forge_container_app`
directly.  Returns 201 on success; 409 if a runner with that name already
exists in the forge namespace.

## CI registry wiring (best-effort, console-internal)

After the CR is created the console automatically:
1. Creates (or rotates) a harbor-scoped service account with the `editor`
   role so CI jobs can pull, push, and delete images within the harbor's
   registry projects.
2. Sets three org-level Forgejo Actions secrets (`REGISTRY_HOST`,
   `REGISTRY_USERNAME`, `REGISTRY_PASSWORD`) so workflow steps can
   `docker login` without any manual configuration.

The registry host (`<org>.rg.<base-domain>`) is injected into
`spec.extra_egress_fqdns` so the operator's `CiliumNetworkPolicy` allows
outbound HTTPS to the registry from inside the Kata microVM.

On clusters with a private platform CA (mkcert / corporate PKI) the
operator additionally mounts the CA cert into the `dind` sidecar at
`/etc/docker/certs.d/<registry_host>/ca.crt`; this is driven by
`spec.registry_host` (set here) and the operator's `platform_ca_cert_b64`.

**Provisioning failures do not roll back the CR.** The runner itself is
functional regardless. If provisioning fails it is logged as a warning;
deleting and re-creating the runner retries it (idempotent via Vault).
The best-effort choice matches the operator's own pattern of decoupling
CR creation from reconciliation: the CR is the authority, wiring is async.

patch.description:
Exists because the alternative — delete and recreate — deregisters the scale
set from GitHub, which drops the `runs-on:` target and interrupts whatever
was running. Every field below can change without that happening.

## What the operator does with each field
- **`min_runners` / `max_runners`** — a live resize. ARC moves the target
  count on the existing `AutoscalingRunnerSet`; no pod is recreated and no
  running job is touched.
- **`flavor` / `runner_image`** — a template change. The runner pod spec is
  rewritten, so jobs already executing finish on the old template and the
  next ones start on the new one. Nothing is killed mid-job.
- **`runner_group`** — re-registers the scale set into another GitHub runner
  group. Brief, and the scale-set name is unchanged, so `runs-on:` keeps
  working.
- **`runs_on`** — deregisters the scale set and registers it again under a
  new name. The one edit here that workflows can see, and the one with
  downtime: GitHub will not move a registration's runner label in place, so
  the `AutoscalingRunnerSet` is deleted and re-applied (its Kubernetes name
  is unchanged, as is every other object). ARC drains in-flight runners
  first, so no job is killed, but the pool accepts nothing until the new
  registration is live, and a workflow still naming the old value queues
  until it is updated. `""` hands the name back to the derived one.
- **`extra_egress_fqdns`** — the pool's network policy is re-rendered. It
  replaces the previous list wholesale rather than merging into it.
- **`connection`** — the pool's config secret is re-projected from the new
  credential. This is the rotation path: swap in a fresh App key or PAT
  without the scale set ever leaving GitHub.

`scope` is deliberately not editable; see [`UpdateGithubRunnerRequest`].

AccessBinding.description:
One access binding at a resource scope, for the resource-anchored "Access"
view (who can do what *here*). A flattened `grants` row joined with the
principal's display name and the role/permission name, so the UI can list
bindings on a resource without N per-principal lookups. Each binding is a
`grants` row, so `grant_id` is what the delete-grant endpoint revokes.

grant_id.description: The `grants` row id — pass to the delete-grant endpoint to revoke.

inherited.description:
`true` when the binding is not attached to exactly this resource but
reaches it through inheritance — an org-wide grant, an ancestor folder,
or a covering wildcard. Inherited bindings are read-only on this resource
(managed on the ancestor they are attached to). Only populated by the
inheritance-aware listing; defaults to `false` for the exact-scope list.

permission_id.description:
Set when the binding confers a single permission; `permission_key` is its
`resource:action` label.

principal_name.description:
Human-readable principal: a user's email or a service account's name
(falls back to the id for an orphaned row).

resource_uuid.description:
Attached-tier anchor: the concrete resource id when bound from the
resource itself (survives a slug rename). `None` = pattern-tier.

role_id.description: Set when the binding confers a whole role bundle; `role_name` is its label.

scope_path.description: The resource path the binding is scoped to (matches the query `scope_path`).

AccessCheckItem.description: One `(action, resource)` pair to test for the caller.

resource_id.description: Resource scope path / HRN id; empty for an org- or collection-level action.

AccessCheckResult.description: The verdict for one checked pair (echoed back so the client can map results).

ActionParameter.description:
One declared parameter of an [`ActionType`] — a named input mapped to a
backing column *through* a property of the target object type
(`property_api_name`), never a raw column. At execution the property
resolves to its `source_column` + `data_type`, and the caller-supplied
value is rendered to a typed SQL literal — the only way a value enters DML.

api_name.description: Machine name the caller uses as the key in `ExecuteActionRequest.parameters`.

data_type.description:
Semantic type driving literal rendering (string/integer/double/...),
re-derived from the resolved property at execution time; carried here so
the definition is self-describing.

property_api_name.description:
The target object type's property this parameter writes — resolved to a
physical `source_column` at execution time.

ActionResult.description:
Result of executing an [`ActionType`] — the DML ran (and was audited via
query history); this reports the outcome, not the affected rows.

ActionType.description:
A governed, parameterized write-back to an object type's backing Iceberg
table — the Kinetic layer's unit. Declares WHAT a write may do (target,
operation, parameter shape); executing it builds ONE constrained DML
statement run through the caller's JWT (Vauban/OPA + Trino authorize the
actual write, and it is recorded in query history). Never arbitrary DML.

api_name.description:
Stable machine name, unique per org. Immutable after creation (same
rationale as [`ObjectType::api_name`]).

parameters.description: Decoded straight from the JSONB `parameters` column.

AiAgentCapabilityResponse.description: One capability, as a client lists it.

capability.description:
The word a user and the CLI use for it (`documents`, `platform-ops`), and the
value to send as `speciality` when creating it. Named for what a user is
choosing rather than for the CR field it lands in.

default_enabled.description:
Whether a client should offer it pre-selected: an agent with no capability
registers no dispatch tool and can answer nothing at all.

description.description:
One line for a client with no copy of its own. English: a client that
translates its own copy (the console) uses that instead.

name.description:
What the capability is called, and what a correspondent sees when it answers
their mail (#3479). Not translated, on purpose — a name that changed with the
locale of whoever created the agent would make that attribution unstable.

needs_data_source.description:
Whether this capability answers from a data source, so a client knows to ask
for one. A `documents` capability created without a dock says "I could not
find anything", which is indistinguishable from an empty corpus.

preamble.description:
The instructions this capability runs with, before the user's own mission is
layered on top. Read-only, and returned for transparency rather than for a
client to echo: `create` composes it, and a caller that sends its own is
taken at its word — which is how the two would drift apart.

tools.description:
The commands and tools this capability is given. Informational — `create`
fills it in — but worth showing: it is the difference between what two
capabilities can actually do.

AiAgentDataSourceDto.description: A data dock the agent may read.

tables.description:
Fully-qualified tables (`catalog.schema.table`) the agent may read in
this dock. Omitted or empty means the whole dock, which is what every
agent created before this field gets.

AiAgentDesiredStateDto.description:
Whether the agent should be running. Stopping and starting is user-driven,
exactly like a container app: there is no autoscaler and no wake-on-request,
so a stopped agent answers nothing until someone starts it.

api_key_secret_id.description:
Id of a Passe Partout secret of type `plaintext` holding the OpenRouter
API key. Required when `provider` is `openrouter`.

endpoint_url.description: TEST-ONLY (#3021): OpenAI-compatible base URL for the `custom` provider.

model.description:
Model selection. For `sapience`: `sapience:shared/<name>` or
`sapience:org/<name>`. For `openrouter`: the bare model id
(e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-chat`).

AiAgentMailDto.description:
Mailbox configuration for the `mail` interface: one account used for both
IMAP (inbound) and SMTP (replies).

Every field below `mode` besides `display_name`/`allowed_senders` is
meaningful, and accepted, **only** in `External` mode (FR6): a `Managed`
payload need not — and, per `validate_mail`, must not — set them.

allowed_senders.description:
Senders the agent answers (substring/domain match against the parsed
address). Empty = answer everyone. Both modes.

display_name.description:
Friendly name recipients see instead of the bare address
(`Support Assistant <agent@example.com>`), so several agents sharing a
domain stay distinguishable. Omit to fall back to the agent's name. Printable
single-line text, at most 64 characters. Both modes.

from_address.description:
From address on replies (usually the mailbox address). External mode
only.

imap_host.description: IMAP server host (e.g. `ssl0.ovh.net`). External mode only.

imap_port.description: IMAP port (993 for implicit TLS). External mode only.

password_secret_id.description:
Id of a Passe Partout secret of type `plaintext` holding the mailbox
password. External mode only.

smtp_host.description: SMTP server host (e.g. `ssl0.ovh.net`). External mode only.

smtp_port.description: SMTP port (465 implicit TLS, 587 STARTTLS). External mode only.

use_tls.description:
TLS on the mail connections; defaults to `true` when omitted. Disable
only for in-cluster dev servers. External mode only — a managed payload
must leave it unset (managed mode is always in-cluster plaintext), and
an explicit value is rejected there like every other external-only
field rather than silently overridden.

username.description:
Login for both IMAP and SMTP (usually the mailbox address). External
mode only.

AiAgentMailModeDto.description:
How the mailbox is provisioned (ADR-0027 / PRD-006). `External` is the
default: the create-agent payload predating this field (or one that omits
`mode`) keeps today's bring-your-own behaviour.

AiAgentMailStatsResponse.description:
Mail activity counters as reported by the agent runtime. In-memory on the
pod: they reset on restart (persistent activity is a later milestone).

enabled.description: Whether the runtime has the mail interface configured.

errors.description:
Messages that could not be handled: an error reply, or a reply given up on
after its send failed repeatedly. NOT incremented while a reply is still
being retried — see `undelivered` for that.

ignored_senders.description: Messages dropped by the sender allowlist.

last_reply_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the last successful reply.

received.description: Messages fetched and processed, whatever the outcome.

undelivered.description:
Replies generated but not yet delivered, waiting on a send that keeps
failing. A gauge, not a counter: it returns to zero when they go out or are
given up on (at which point `errors` counts one).

`serde(default)` so a console talking to an agent from before this field
existed — mid-rollout — reads zero instead of failing the whole response.

AiAgentMailStatusDto.description:
Mail runtime state (PRD-006 FR7): mode, resolved address, and — managed
mode only — a phase/message mirroring the owned `MailAccount`. Read-only,
sourced verbatim from `AiAgent.status.mail` (the console never talks to
Stalwart, ADR-0027 §2).

address.description:
The address the agent is reachable at. `None` in managed mode until
the mailbox is provisioned.

AiAgentMailboxPhaseDto.description:
Managed-mode mailbox phase (PRD-006 FR7), mirroring the owned
`MailAccount`'s status.

AiAgentMemoryResponse.description:
Whether this agent has its conversation memory, as the POD reports it.

Deliberately not read from `AiAgent.status.sessions`, which the operator
publishes: that says what the platform provisioned and mounted, this says
whether the pod can use it, and the two have been measured disagreeing in both
directions — a Ready database and role no pod could reach, and unreadable
credentials on pods that were connected and remembering fine. The console asks
the pod, because the pod is the only one that knows.
`Default` is "no memory reported", which is what an agent pod from before this
block existed means — see `RuntimeStats::sessions`.

configured.description:
Whether a conversation database was configured for this agent at all.

Separate from `connected` so the console can tell "this harbour has no
conversation database, as configured" from "it has one and this agent cannot
reach it". With one flag, an agent that was never given a database would read
as broken forever.

`serde(default)` so a console talking to an agent from before this field
existed — mid-rollout — reads false instead of failing the whole response.

connected.description:
Whether it is connected right now. `true` means this agent remembers the
conversation it is in.

slug.description:
This agent's URL-safe identifier: its display name, slugified.

Exposed because `subagent_of` is resolved against this value, so a caller
attaching a capability to this agent needs the identifier the platform will look
for. The alternative — re-implementing `slugify` in the caller — puts that rule in
two languages, and a disagreement between them leaves a capability waiting forever
for a parent that does not exist.

Named `slug` rather than after the object it happens to name: an external API
should not teach a caller the platform's internals, and the value is a slug
whatever stores it (review on #3485).

The console-side identity of the watched resource — the same value the
Monitoring page resolves to a `MonitoringTarget` for this kind.

A rule plus its live evaluation, so the UI never has to reconstruct

(console UI, CLI) renders the same thing without duplicating the rule.

AlertablePanelDto.description:

Defaults to `"<destination_prefix>/quarantine/"` when not set.

max_llm_rpm.description: This organization's own ceilings for this key (ADR-0040), editable here.

platform_max_llm_rpm.description:
The platform admin's cap on this key. Read-only for the tenant, and
shown rather than hidden: a key silently capped below what its owner
set would produce refusals nobody in the org could explain.

AppProtocol.description:
L7 protocol of a `ContainerApp` port, mapping to `ServicePort.appProtocol`
using the values gateways recognise.

Only HTTP for now: the platform ingress terminates HTTP(S) and there is no
listener for anything else. `TCPRoute`/`UDPRoute` exposure arrives with the
Cilium 1.20 upgrade (#3769), which is when this enum grows.

singleton.description: Run-once: at most one instance of this template may exist per environment.

AppUsageRef.description:
Reference to a ContainerApp that has a custom domain under this apex.

Populated by walking the org namespace's ContainerApps and matching FQDNs that
fall under the apex. Empty in list responses; populated on detail.

containerAppId.description: Console DB id of the ContainerApp. `None` before the operator's first reconcile.

fqdn.description: Specific FQDN under this apex declared on the ContainerApp's `customDomains`.

name.description: Container app slug (also the CRD name in the org namespace).

AppliedProposal.description:
Result of persisting an [`OntologyProposal`] — counts only, not the
created rows themselves (the caller re-lists if it needs them). An
existing `api_name` (object type or link type) is skipped rather than
failing the whole batch, so re-applying a proposal after editing it is
safe.

properties_skipped.description:
Properties dropped by the apply-side sanitation (invalid `api_name`,
or belonging to a dropped object type).

ApplyOntologyProposalRequest.description:
Body for `POST /ontology/apply` — the reviewed proposal plus the
grounding (data dock/catalog/schema) every object type it creates is
stamped with.

destination_bucket_name.description: Staging bucket the exported archive is written to (same Harbor).

prefix.description: Prefix filtering which objects are included in the archive.

strip_prefix.description: Whether to strip the prefix from paths inside the archive.

destination_bucket_name.description: Staging bucket the archive was uploaded to (from prepare).

file_path.description: Full path to the uploaded archive (from the prepare response).

prefix.description: Optional prefix files are extracted under in the target bucket.

session_id.description:
Conversation this question belongs to, so the agent can answer with the
history of the exchange rather than treating every message as the first.

Omit it to start a new conversation — the response carries the id that was
minted, and sending it back on the next question continues the thread. Mail
needs no equivalent: it derives its conversation from the message headers.

This id IS the conversation's key: the same value comes back from
`GET …/sessions` and addresses the transcript and delete routes. Typed as a
`Uuid` so a value the read routes could not accept is rejected here rather
than reaching the agent.

The conversation this answer belongs to — either the id the caller sent, or
a freshly minted one. Echoed so a client that did not supply one still ends
up with a conversation it can continue, and so the id format has a single
authority rather than every caller inventing its own.

AssistantAnswer.description:
The assistant's grounded answer plus machine-usable pointers the UI turns
into one-click chips: `suggested_object_types`/`suggested_actions` are
`api_name`s that MUST exist in the model (the server drops any the LLM
invents before returning — same defence-in-depth posture as
`sanitize_proposal`).

AssistantRequest.description:
A natural-language question about the org's ontology. The assistant is
grounded ONLY on the semantic definitions (object types, properties, links,
actions) — pure console-DB metadata, no Trino — so it can answer "how do
Patient and Encounter relate?" or "what can I do to an Encounter?" and point
the user at the right object type / action to open next. It resolves no
instances itself; navigating to real rows stays the (JWT-governed) instance
layer's job.

model.description:
Model override, same contract as [`GenerateOntologyRequest::model`];
`None` uses the deployment's configured copilot model.

BackupOrigin.description:
Whether the backup was user-initiated or produced by a scheduled run that
the operator adopted. Mirrored into the DB column `origin` (VARCHAR(16)
with a CHECK constraint on the same vocabulary) and into the OpenAPI spec
as an `enum`, so every consumer (operator via progenitor, frontend via
hey-api, SDK users) sees the same closed set.

Delivery kinds, all three delivered end to end. The two webhook kinds share
one transport (an HTTPS POST to a capability URL) and differ only in payload

Maps result-set columns to visual channels. Which fields matter depends on
the chart type (`stat` reads `value`, `pie` reads `category`+`value`,
cartesian charts read `x`+`y`).

Bounded chart vocabulary, kept close to Vega-Lite mark semantics so the
renderer can be swapped without respecifying every dashboard.

Create the branch from the current HEAD instead of switching to an
existing one (`git checkout -b`).

API key for the AI model (e.g., Mistral), as a literal.

Optional since #3691: a caller may send `api_key_secret` instead, and
exactly one of the two is required. It stays a plain string so every
client written before the secret form keeps working unchanged.

max_content_chars.description:
Hard cap on document content (in chars) sent to the LLM per request.
Oversize content is reduced via map-reduce summarization. Uses the
executor's library default (120_000) when absent.

The cap is in characters while the model bounds its input in tokens, so
the safe value depends on the corpus: dense text (OCR'd accounting
tables, amounts, dates, accented French) costs more tokens per character
than the default assumes, and the default then overflows the context
window. Lower it for such a corpus; raise it for a wider-context model.

model_base_url.description:
Base URL for the model API. Defaults to Mistral API when not set.
Set to a vLLM/KServe endpoint for self-hosted models (e.g., "http://ministral-3-8b-rocm-predictor.kserve.svc.cluster.local/v1").

operator. Deliberately typed rather than passed through as raw JSON: this is
the only per-partition readiness signal the console and `hfctl` have.

name.description: Partition name, matching the dock's CRD spec.

ready_nodes.description:
Compute nodes currently `Ready`.

The alias is load-bearing: the operator serialises the CRD's
`PartitionStatus` into the jsonb column, and that type is camelCase. No
`serde(default)` on purpose — a shape this can no longer read must
surface as "no counts yet", never as a confident `0`.

ComputeEngineInput.description:
Compute engine backing the dock. v1 ships `Slurm` only; the enum is the
extension point for a future engine, mirroring the CRD's `ComputeEngine`.

oneOf.description:
Applies only if the principal carries attribute `key` with `value` among
its values. Sourced from the identity: curated claims (`email`,
`email_domain`, `client_id`) and the user's per-org RLS attributes
(`namespace::value`, grouped by namespace — e.g. `region == "occitanie"`).

Applies only if the request context carries attribute `key` with `value`
among its values — attributes projected from the call's own payload at
decision time (e.g. a secret's `secret_type`, or one of its `tag`s).

Condition.description:
An optional predicate that gates whether a grant applies, evaluated at
decision time against the principal's attributes (ABAC) or the request
context derived from the call's payload.

The tagged representation lets new context sources be added without
reshaping stored grants. Matching is membership-based: a key may carry
multiple values (a user holding `region::occitanie` and `region::paris`, or
a create request tagging several labels), and the condition holds when
`value` is among them.

ConditionView.description:
Generic Kubernetes-style condition surfaced to the console UI.

Mirrors the shape used on `OrgStorageStatus.conditions` and
`HarborStorageBindingStatus.conditions`. The CRD-side enums for
`type_` are flattened to plain strings (the variant names) so the
frontend can render unknown future condition types without a code
update.

ConnectorDescriptorResponse.description:
Static description of one opendata connector: slug, human title, a one-line
summary, catalog facets (category + region), and the JSON Schema of the
connector's params used to drive the dynamic UI form.

bonus_cpu_millis.description:
The free burst above the sold envelope, in millicores
(`cpu_limit millis - entitlement_cpu_millis`), read directly off the live
`cpu_limit`/entitlement — not re-derived from `CaasTierConfig` ratios, which
would be undefined for a `resource_tier: null` app. `None` when the spec
renders no explicit CPU limit (nothing to compute a ceiling from) or failed
to parse.

entitlement_cpu_millis.description:
What this app's live CRD spec sells, in millicores — `resources.entitlement.cpu`
via `footprint_from_spec` (ADR-0012 `× replicas`), with the same pre-#3628
fallback to `resources.requests.cpu` `footprint_from_spec` applies. Populated
even when `resource_tier` is `None` (a legacy CRD or a custom entitlement that
doesn't match any tier on the table exactly) — self-sufficient for the detail
screen so it never has to invent a sold number from the catalog (#3631).

expose_to_internet.description:
Whether internet-facing routes are enabled for this app. Reflects the live CRD
value so the edit dialog can prefill the current state.

port.description:
**Deprecated — read `ports`.** The primary port, or the raw

exists — a raw TCP/UDP app has no port to single out.

ports.description:

already folded in — an app that has never been edited since `ports`
landed still reports one entry here.

resource_version.description:
The Kubernetes resourceVersion of this object at read time.
Must be round-tripped verbatim as `resource_version` in PATCH requests
to enable optimistic concurrency control; the server returns 409 Conflict
when the live object has advanced past this version.

starting.description:

"ContainerCreating", "CrashLoopBackOff", "ImagePullBackOff",
"ContainersNotReady". None when `ready == true`.

table (subject to opt-in migration). Empty for schemas.

The user's own instructions for a CAPABILITY, layered on top of the catalogue
preamble in `system_prompt` — which, for a capability, is the console's rather
than the user's. Kept separate so the runtime composes the two in a fixed order
and user text cannot contradict the tool subset the capability was given (#3477).

Agent name (unique within the organization; slugified for the CR name).

Optional for a CAPABILITY: a request naming `subagent_of` and a `speciality`
the platform offers is named `"<agent name> <capability name>"`, so what a
capability is called does not depend on which client created it. Required for
anything else.

Hyperfluid Service-Account entity id the agent authenticates as. Must
be viewer-scoped. Optional at creation.

a router's prompt IS the user's own mission.

`hfctl:<command>`. An empty array means every tool and command.

the `speciality` comes with: the capability's own from the catalogue, or
`ask_sender` + `ask_subagent` for `routing`.

table the connector data is loaded into.

pointing at an **external** system. Required for every connector kind
the registry has a descriptor for, unless the kind is `Postgresql` and
`managed_postgresql_user_id` is given instead.

One field for all 29 external connectors of epic #3559, rather than one
optional field per connector: the bundle's *shape* is per-connector and
lives in the registry
(`GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/trino/connectors`), not in this DTO.

The console reads the secret once, here, only to validate it against
that descriptor — so an unusable bundle is a 400 naming the field
rather than a `Terminal` condition the user discovers minutes later.

org-scoped, at every reconcile.

it for any other kind is a 400 rather than being ignored, so a
mistargeted request fails loudly instead of silently producing an
unconfigured catalog.

Must be a read-only (`viewer`) user of a DBaaS cluster in the same
organization, already synced on the cluster
(`observed_permission_level = viewer`) — the console derives the
connection secret from the user's CRD status, so arbitrary secrets
can't be linked. Mirrors

  synced, read-only (`viewer`) user may back it, the same contract the
  legacy `POST /data-containers/postgresql` endpoint enforces (see
  `resolve_viewer_backed_secret`).
* `connection_secret_name` — a database Hyperfluid does not operate,

cannot express "fit in what I can read". A dozen hits are a few kilobytes on a
corpus of notes and 60 KB on a corpus of PDFs. The budget belongs to the
consumer — how much context it has — rather than to the data (#3234).

stored: it is derived from each permission's family at projection time, so a
grant can't drift from the permission it gates.

resource_uuid.description:
Two-tier key. `Some` = ATTACHED tier: bound to one concrete resource by
its immutable DB id, so it survives a slug rename and is cascade-GC'd by
exact uuid match on that resource's delete (and `scope_path` is that
resource's exact path, never a wildcard). `None` = PATTERN tier: keyed
only by `scope_path`. Never enters the OPA projection — GC/identity only.

scope_path.description:
A path in the org's resource tree the grant is scoped to: exact, an
ancestor folder (matches descendants), or a `*`-suffixed wildcard. `None`
= org-wide. The enforcement key the OPA projection composes into an HRN.

Group.description:
A named, org-scoped collection of principals. Binding an access level to a
group (a [`Grant`] with `principal_type = "group"` and `principal_id` = this
id) applies that access to every member, resolved through the OPA projection.

member_count.description:
Number of principals (users + service accounts) in the group. Computed by
every group-returning query via a correlated count, so it is always
populated — a query that omits it fails loudly in `FromRow` rather than
silently reporting 0.

GroupMember.description:
One member of a [`Group`]: a polymorphic principal (a user or a service
account), keyed the same way `grants` keys a principal. Carries the
principal's human-readable name so the management UI can list members without
an N+1 lookup.

principal_name.description: A user's email or a service account's name (falls back to the id).

bucket_name.description:
Tenant-prefixed bucket name materialized by the operator on RGW
(i.e. `.status.bucket_name`). Equals `name` for non-prefixed
deployments; surfaced separately so the UI can show what the
underlying object store actually sees. `None` while the operator
has not yet stamped the status field.

endpoint.description: External HTTPS S3 endpoint URL clients use to reach this bucket.

freeze_writes.description: True when writes are administratively frozen on this bucket.

object_count.description: Object count. `None` if storage stats are temporarily unavailable.

quota_gb.description:
Effective per-bucket quota in GB actually enforced on RGW: an explicit
`spec.quotaGb` override if set, otherwise the org-wide default. `None`
means no quota is enforced (genuinely unlimited).

quota_is_default.description:
True when `quota_gb` reflects the org-wide default rather than an
explicit per-bucket override (the bucket has no `spec.quotaGb` and
inherits `OrgStorage.defaultPerBucketQuotaGb`). Lets the UI show the
inherited value without pinning it as an override on save.

region.description:
S3-protocol region clients must sign with. This is the RGW zonegroup
`api_name` the backend signs SigV4 against (`"default"`), **not** a
physical location — surfaced so SDKs can be configured correctly.

s3_gateway_enabled.description:
True when this bucket's zone runs an S3 gateway, i.e. when a session
could actually be minted for it. Resolved with the SAME predicate the
session endpoint enforces, so the console cannot offer a credential the
server would refuse — nor hide one it would grant.

size_bytes.description:
Cumulative size in bytes. `None` if storage stats are temporarily
unavailable.

zone_id.description: Storage zone the bucket lives in (`"default"` for the primary).

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the HFBucket CR was created in the cluster.

ready.description: True when the operator has marked the bucket as Ready in `.status`.

zone_id.description: Storage zone the bucket lives in (`"default"` for the primary).

Harbor.description:
A harbor is a collection of [DataDocks](super::datadock::Datadock)
Each harbor belongs to an [Org](super::org::Org)
Each harbor has an owner who is a [User](super::user::User)

namespace.description:
Dedicated Kubernetes workload namespace for this harbor (ADR-0031).
`None` = legacy shared placement in `hf-{org}`. Stamped at INSERT only
when the owning organization opted in (`dedicated_harbor_namespaces`);
the stored value is the single source of truth — always READ, never
recomputed.

HarborRef.description: Reference to the harbor (environment/project) this link belongs to.

name.description: Name of the harbor.

namespace.description:
Namespace of the Harbor CR — the org plane (`hf-{org}`), where the
Harbor and org storage stay even when a harbor gets its own dedicated
workload namespace (ADR-0031). The operator resolves org identity and
RGW targets there. `None` = the link's own namespace, i.e. harbors that
still share `hf-{org}`.

conditions.description:
Full set of `.status.conditions` from the HarborStorageBinding CRD,
surfaced to the UI so operators can see per-subsystem state
(OrgStorageReady, TenantEnsured, OwnerUserEnsured, StsRoleReady).

zone_id.description: Storage zone this tenant lives in (`"default"` for the primary).

HealthThresholds.description:
What "too small", "too many deletes" and "too much history" currently mean
for this catalog.

from_schedule.description:
True when these came from the catalog's own maintenance schedule rather
than from the defaults.

small_file_threshold_bytes.description:
Derived from the schedule's `compact_files.file_size_threshold`, or the
platform default when no schedule exists.

HistogramBucketDto.description:
A single volume-histogram bucket — a line count for one fixed time bucket.
Powers the logs explorer's volume-over-time bar chart above the entries
(ADR-0020). Unlike the sources facet, the histogram DOES reflect the active
search/level/pod/container filters and the query window.

count.description: Number of matching log lines in this bucket.

IcebergHealthReport.description: The health list, plus the verdict of the catalog as a whole.

tables.description: Worst first, then stalest — the order someone reading top-down wants.

tables_total.description: `None` until the sweep has finished listing the catalog.

oldest_measured_at.description: Oldest measurement in the set: how far behind the whole picture is.

reclaimable_files.description:
Data files compaction could plausibly remove, summed over tables that
need it.

small_files_total.description:
Small data files across the catalog — the raw size of the compaction
backlog.

tables_needing_attention_out_of_scope.description:
Tables that need attention and that the maintenance schedule does not
cover — work the nightly run will never do, however green it looks.

exclude_patterns.description: Glob patterns excluded after `include_patterns` has been applied.

include_patterns.description: Glob patterns matched against `schema.table`. Empty means every table.

max_duration_minutes.description:
Wall-clock budget for a run. `None` means unbounded, which is also what
every pre-existing config has.

max_parallel_tables.description: How many tables the runner may optimize concurrently.

skip_unchanged.description:
Skip a table whose current snapshot is the one the last successful run
already optimized.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration measured by the runner.

finished_reason.description:
Set when the terminal status did not come from the runner itself (today:
the stuck-run reaper).

pod_name.description:
Pod that executed the run, as it reported itself. Scopes the log query;
`None` means the run never got far enough to register.

IcebergOptimizeSummary.description:
Rolling outcome of a catalog's maintenance, over the summary window.

Everything here is derived from runs the console recorded, not from the
metrics store: the runner is a batch pod that is gone by the time anyone
looks, so its outcome numbers are reported to us and kept, rather than
scraped.

avg_duration_ms.description:
Median-free on purpose: the average is what a capacity conversation
uses, and a single run's outlier is visible in the history right below.

bytes_reclaimed.description:
Storage the window's runs handed back, i.e. sum of `bytes_before -
bytes_after` over runs where both were measured. Can be negative:
compaction rewrites files and a run can legitimately end up larger.

files_removed.description: Files merged away, same basis as `bytes_reclaimed`.

runs_running.description: Runs still in flight (or never terminated) at read time.

window_days.description: Length of the window these totals cover.

annotations.description:
Annotations mirrored from the `TrinoSchema` CRD metadata when
`source = Crd`. Empty otherwise.

IcebergTableHealth.description:
One table, measured and graded.

The raw measurement travels with the verdict on purpose: a badge nobody can
check is a badge nobody believes, and the numbers are what make "compact
this" an argument rather than an instruction.

avg_data_file_bytes.description: Mean data file size — the number the compaction target is set against.

compacted_file_estimate.description:
Roughly how few data files compaction could leave behind. A floor, not
a promise: Iceberg will not merge across partitions.

in_maintenance_scope.description:
Whether the catalog's maintenance schedule would touch this table.

A fragmented table its own schedule excludes is the finding nobody goes
looking for: the maintenance page says everything succeeded, because
everything it was allowed to touch did.

measured_by.description:
`scan` (an on-demand sweep) or `run` (a maintenance run reporting the
state it left the table in).

partial_measurement.description:
True when only the basic `$files` aggregate could be read, so
file-content-dependent findings could not be evaluated at all. The
severity then covers less than it appears to, and the UI says so.

short_name.description: Bare table name, split out so the UI does not have to parse the FQN.

small_file_ratio.description: Share of data files below the threshold, `0..1`.

small_file_threshold_bytes.description:
The threshold this measurement's small-file count was taken against.
Shown so a reader can tell a stale grading from a current one.

table_name.description: `catalog.schema.table` — the same string a maintenance run reports.

IcebergTableMetadata.description: Iceberg table metadata stored in Hyperfluid

annotations.description:
Metadata annotations copied from the CRD when `source = Crd`. The UI
surfaces well-known keys (e.g. `hyperfluid.nudibranches.tech/source`,
`hyperfluid.nudibranches.tech/pipeline`) as coloured badges.

IdentityProvider.description:
A brokered identity provider as returned to API callers. The client secret
is deliberately absent — it is write-only and lives only in Keycloak.

oidc_base_url.description: Issuer/base URL, present only for a custom OIDC provider.

IdentityProviderKind.description: Which external identity provider a broker federates to.

ImageScan.description:
A persisted image scan — one row per `(registry_id, digest)`. The `report`
is the full Trivy JSON; the read-views and the API surface only the summary
projection ([`ScanSummary`]).

report.description: Full Trivy JSON report; `None` until published / on failure.

severity_max.description:
Most severe non-empty bucket as the canonical UPPERCASE token
(`CRITICAL`/`HIGH`/…); `None` when clean or not yet scanned.

ca_cert.description: Optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS verification

catch_all.description: Whether to process all messages (true) or only those with attachments (false)

use_tls.description: Use TLS (default: true). Set to false for plain IMAP, e.g. local dev without certs.

ImportApiExtraFilter.description: Filter on a field within the `extra` JSON object returned by the Import API.

destination_prefix.description: Optional prefix path within the destination bucket

destination_prefix.description: Optional prefix path within the destination bucket

harbor_id.description: Harbor UUID that owns the bucket

InboundEmailDestinationConfig.description:
S3 destination for an inbound email pipeline.

Two variants are accepted:

* **`DataContainer`** (legacy) — a `DataContainerBucket` UUID from Postgres.

* **`HarborBucket`** (ADR-0008) — an `HFBucket` CRD name under a Harbor UUID.
  The bucket must exist and be Ready. No legacy fallback.

InboundEmailExtractionConfig.description: Optional extraction step appended after landing attachments to S3 in an inbound email pipeline

ocr_api_key.description: API key for Mistral OCR. Required when ocr_provider is Mistral (the default).

InboundEmailSecurityConfig.description:
Security policy applied to every email, regardless of transport.
Verdicts from SPF/DKIM/DMARC are always surfaced in attachment metadata so downstream
consumers can apply their own policy on top of whatever the pipeline enforces.

allowed_content_types.description:
If set, only these MIME content-types are accepted.
Takes precedence over `blocked_content_types`.

blocked_content_types.description:
MIME content-types that are always rejected (e.g. `["application/x-msdownload"]`).
Matched as a prefix so `"application/x-"` blocks all `application/x-*` types.

max_attachment_bytes.description: Maximum size in bytes for a single attachment. `null` = unlimited.

max_email_bytes.description: Maximum total raw email size in bytes. `null` = unlimited.

oneOf.description: Poll an IMAP mailbox for new messages

InboundEmailSourceConfig.description:
Transport-agnostic inbound email source configuration.
The transport variant determines how emails are physically received.

InstancePage.description: A page of instances plus the cursor echoed back and whether more rows exist.

has_more.description:
`true` when the backing table has at least one more row past this page
(computed by over-fetching one row, so it needs no `COUNT(*)`).

IntendedUse.description: What the requester intends to use the trial for.

InvitationIdentityProvider.description:
An identity provider offered on the invitation page, so the invitee can
sign in through it instead of setting a password. Only the fields the public
invite page needs — never any secret.

rotate.description:
Without this a re-issue returns the same credential: a derived key is a
pure function of `(ring, tenant, subject, epoch)`.

permissions.description:
The S3 verbs to grant, shared across every bucket in `scopes`, as
permission keys (e.g. `bucket:read_objects`). Must be a non-empty subset
of the data-plane verbs; control-plane verbs are refused.

scopes.description:
The buckets (and, per bucket, optional prefixes within it) the key is
confined to. At least one is required. Every bucket here is resolved
under the SAME gateway target (see `issue_scoped_s3_key`'s doc comment)
-- one zone, one Ceph tenant -- so they must all live in that one zone;
the frontend enforces this by only offering same-zone buckets.

endpoint.description:
A long-lived key is only valid at the gateway; presenting it to RGW
answers `InvalidAccessKeyId`.
A long-lived key is only valid at the gateway; RGW answers `InvalidAccessKeyId`.

service_account_id.description:
The dedicated, customer-owned service account created to carry this key's
grants. Revoke the key, or delete this account, to end the credential.

KafkaMetadata.description: Dynamic metadata about the Kafka cluster (stored as JSONB)

KpiThreshold.description:
A colored KPI threshold (issue #2959): when the stat value crosses `at`,
render it in `color`.

description.description: Human-readable description for LLM classification

id.description: Unique identifier for this label

Label.description:
Full label definition supporting both static and dynamic types.
This is the primary type used for document classification labels.

Example YAML:
```yaml
# Static label
- id: facture_eau
  type: static
  description: "Water utility invoices"

# Dynamic label with placeholders
- id: travaux
  type: dynamic
  description: "Construction work documents"
  format: "TRAVAUX/{year}/{date}-{work_name}"
  placeholders:
    - id: year
      source: "Extract the year from the document"
      format: "YYYY"
      rules: ["Must be 4 digits"]
```

oneOf.description: Static label - fixed category path
Dynamic label - category path with extracted placeholders

LabelType.description: Label type - either static or dynamic with placeholders

LinkType.description:
A typed, directed relationship between two Object Types — the analogue of
a JOIN between their backing tables. Relationships are modelled
explicitly, never inferred.

ListContextProvidersResponse.description: Response for list of context providers.

ListContextualRestrictionsResponse.description: Response for list of contextual restrictions.

common_prefixes.description: Immediate sub-directory names under `current_path` (single-level listings only).

current_path.description: The prefix the server used to compute this listing (echoed back for the UI).

total.description: Total number of secrets matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

ListTableClassificationsResponse.description: Response for list of table classifications.

ListUserAttributesResponse.description: Response containing a list of user attributes.

LogLevel.description:
Log severity filter (ADR-0020, Decision 3).

Maps to a STATIC LogsQL clause (see `logsql::level_clause`) — it never
interpolates user text, so it adds zero injection surface. The mapping is a
case-insensitive prefix-token heuristic over the unstructured message text
(platform binaries do not emit structured levels — see the ADR non-goals),
so false positives (a line merely containing the word "error") are accepted.

LogSourceDto.description:
A (pod, container) log source in scope, with a hit count — powers the logs
explorer's source dropdown (ADR-0020). Independent of the active
search/level/source filters so the dropdown stays stable.

LogStream.description:
CRI log stream a line was emitted on. Maps to a STATIC exact `stream:="…"`
LogsQL filter (the value comes from this closed enum, never user text).

ManagedMailConfigResponse.description:
Managed agent-mail availability (ADR-0027 / PRD-006). Contract with the
console wizard — keep this exact shape: `enabled` is always present,
`domain` is the platform mail domain (e.g. `"agents.acme-cloud.eu"`) and
`null` when managed mail is disabled.

domain.description:
Domain managed mailboxes are provisioned under. `null` iff `enabled`
is false.

enabled.description:
True when the platform is configured for managed mailboxes
(`HF_MAIL_DOMAIN` set on the console).

MedallionTier.description: Medallion architecture tiers for data lake house governance

MessageAttachment.description:
One image attached to a user turn. The BFF re-encodes it as the `data:`
URL `file` part opencode expects — verified on opencode 1.18.18: a
`{ type: "file", mime, filename, url: "data:<mime>;base64,…" }` part is
accepted on `/session/{id}/message`, stored verbatim in the message list,
and handed to the model as an image.

data.description: Raw bytes, standard base64 (NO `data:` prefix). Decoded size ≤ 5 MiB.

filename.description: Original file name, shown in the transcript. Sanitized before forwarding.

MessageAuthorKind.description:
Which side of the boundary wrote a message. This — not a flag on the
request — is what the derived status transition reads.

oneOf.description: Prose (markdown).

id.description:
opencode part id (`prt_...`). Optional for back-compat: rows from an
older BFF omit it and the reducer falls back to append-only ordering.

oneOf.description: Model reasoning / thinking trace.

id.description: opencode part id (`prt_...`); see `Text::id`.

oneOf.description: A tool invocation: read / edit / write / bash / grep / glob / list / ...

call_id.description:
opencode tool-call id (`call_...`, `part.callID`). Lets a pending
interactive request (e.g. the `question` tool) be matched back to
the message part it came from, so the UI can render the prompt
inline in the thread.

id.description: opencode part id (`prt_...`); see `Text::id`.

output.description: Tool output text, truncated to keep payloads sane.

oneOf.description: A filesystem patch the agent applied; lists the changed files.

id.description: opencode part id (`prt_...`); see `Text::id`.

oneOf.description:
A file attached to the turn — today the images a user pastes or drops
in the composer. The BYTES stay out of the message list: opencode stores
them as a `data:` URL on the part, and a thread with a few screenshots
would re-download megabytes on every refetch during a turn. When
`embedded` is true they are served by
`GET …/messages/{mid}/parts/{pid}/content` instead.

embedded.description:
True when opencode holds the bytes with the message (`data:` URL) —
i.e. the part-content endpoint can serve them. False for parts that
only reference a path (`file://` @-mentions from other clients).

id.description: opencode part id (`prt_...`); also the `{pid}` of the content endpoint.

mime.description: MIME type as opencode recorded it (e.g. `image/png`).

size.description: Decoded size in bytes, when the content is embedded.

MessagePart.description:
One renderable piece of an agent turn. opencode emits a rich part stream
(prose, reasoning, tool calls, filesystem patches); we surface the agentic
ones so the UI can show what the agent DID — files read/edited, commands
run, diffs applied — not just its final prose. `kind` is the discriminator.

MetadataStorageConfig.description: Metadata storage configuration (Trino/Iceberg for document metadata)

data_container_id.description: Data Container ID for the Iceberg catalog (DataDock is resolved automatically)

MetricsRange.description: Time range selector for metrics and logs queries.

ModelConfig.description: Extra configuration for the model serving instance.

extraArgs.description: Extra CLI arguments passed to the runtime

storageUri.description: Custom storage URI (e.g. s3:// or pvc://)

ModelOption.description:
A model the user can run a turn on. `id` is the "providerID/modelID" string
the message POST forwards to opencode. The list is opencode's OWN view
(`GET /config/providers`) filtered to the workstation's configured inference
provider, so every entry is by construction a model opencode can resolve —
the entrypoint registers the provider's full catalogue in opencode's config
(`dev-workstations/image/entrypoint.sh`, `configure_opencode_provider`).

attachment.description: The model accepts image input (attachments are handed to it).

context.description: Context window length, when the provider reports it.

id.description: "providerID/modelID", e.g. "openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet".

is_default.description:
True for the model opencode falls back to when a turn sends no explicit
`model`: opencode's configured `model` (which the entrypoint sets from the
workstation's `inference.model`, else its curated default). Read live from
this workstation's opencode, so it is always this workstation's default.
The picker uses it to name + pre-select the default instead of a generic
"Auto" entry.

provider.description:
opencode provider id: "sapience" (in-cluster / local) or "openrouter"
(remote). The picker groups on it.

provider_name.description:
Provider display name as opencode reports it ("OpenRouter",
"Sapience (in-cluster)"), for the picker's group heading.

reasoning.description: The model emits a reasoning trace.

tool_call.description: The model can call tools — an agentic turn needs this.

ModelResources.description: Resource requests for the model serving instance.

ModelRuntime.description: Runtime engine for serving the model.

enabled.description:
`false` when the workload has been stopped (#3712) — still listed,
still deletable, holding no GPU.

message.description:
The human sentence behind [`Self::phase`]. For an unschedulable pod
this is the SCHEDULER's own message, carried verbatim so the console
can show it without kubectl (#3711).

name.description: CRD resource name

reason.description:
Machine-readable reason behind [`Self::phase`] — `Unschedulable`,
`GpuBudgetExceeded`, `NotEntitled`… `None` while nothing is wrong.

ModelType.description: The type of model being served.

ModelUsageTimePoint.description:
One point of the consumption-over-time series, for a single model.

`ts` is the bucket timestamp (unix secs) — the hour start for the History
rollup, the step end for Realtime. A bucket carries one point per model that
saw traffic, so the chart can draw a series per model; a model with no usage
in a bucket is simply absent from it.

NetworkIsolationView.description:
East-west posture of a harbor, surfaced to the UI so the topology page can
frame ServiceLinks as enforced (`strict`) or additive (`lenient`). Mirrors
`HarborSpec::network_isolation` on the Harbor CRD.

NodeTier.description:
Predefined resource tiers for the Dagster webserver/daemon pods.
Memory request and limit are always equal.

NormalizedMessage.description:
A chat message in the stable shape the React panel renders. The BFF
normalizes opencode's `{ info, parts }` envelope into this so the frontend
never has to know opencode's wire schema (and so an opencode upgrade can't
silently reshape the chat). `content` stays for a quick text-only render;
`parts` carries the full ordered agentic stream.

completed.description:
Whether opencode marked the message finished (`info.time.completed`).
`false` on the assistant message of a turn still streaming — the UI
uses this to decide which message hosts the live thinking indicator,
so a follow-up send can't briefly animate the PREVIOUS turn's message.

content.description: Concatenated text of every `text` part, in order.

cost.description: Cost in USD for the turn, if reported.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp derived from opencode's `info.time.created` (epoch ms).

error.description:
Human-readable failure of the turn, when opencode aborted it
(`info.error`, e.g. a provider rejecting the API key). The UI renders it
as an error callout in the assistant bubble — without this, a failed
turn shows as an EMPTY assistant message and looks like a mystery
instead of an actionable error.

id.description: Opencode message id (`msg_...`).

parts.description: Ordered agentic parts: prose, reasoning, tool calls, patches.

tokens.description: Total tokens for the turn, if opencode reported a step-finish.

recipients.description: Email channels only. Empty means "the organization's admins".

url_masked.description:
Webhook channels only, and deliberately truncated — the full URL is a
credential.

ObjectInstance.description:
One resolved row of an object type's backing table, keyed by property
`api_name` (not physical column) so the shape matches the semantic model.

primary_key.description:
Value of the primary-key column for this row — the handle used to fetch
this instance or traverse a link from it.

properties.description: `property api_name -> value` for every source-column-mapped property.

title.description:
The `is_title` property's value when the object type designates one — a
human label for the instance (e.g. a patient's name).

ObjectType.description:
A class of business entity (Customer, Invoice, Flight...), optionally
grounded to one Iceberg table (`backing_*`, all nullable — a type can be
authored as a pure concept first).

api_name.description:
Stable machine name, unique per org — the identity consumers/SDKs bind
to. Immutable after creation (mirrors why `Label.key`/`value` are
mutable but an Object Type's `api_name` is not: renaming it would
break every Link Type and external SDK reference to it).

ObjectTypeWithProperties.description:
[`ObjectType`] plus its [`PropertyDefinition`]s — what `get_object_type`
returns, so a single call gets the whole shape of the type.

oneOf.description: Use Mistral OCR API (api_key from ClassificationConfig.api_key)
Use a local vLLM OCR model (e.g. DeepSeek-OCR on GPU)

text_layer_fastpath.description:
When true, extract the embedded PDF text layer per page and skip OCR
for pages that already have enough text. Opt-in; defaults to false.

OcrProviderConfig.description: OCR provider configuration for PDF processing

OntologyProposal.description:
The full AI-proposed semantic model, returned by `generate` and the
request body `apply` persists (after the user has reviewed/edited it).

notes.description: Copilot commentary (assumptions, caveats), shown to the reviewer.

dataset_id.description: Dataset identifier from the open data catalog (e.g., "rnic")

OptimizeOperationResult.description: One operation (compaction, expiry, orphan removal, analyze) on one table.

OptimizeRunMetrics.description: Run-level totals across every table the run touched.

budget_exhausted.description: True when the run stopped starting tables because it hit its budget.

tables_skipped.description: Tables skipped because nothing changed since the last successful run.

OptimizeStatusAck.description: Whether a report actually moved a row.

OptimizeTableResult.description:
What one table looked like before and after its operations ran.

Trino's `ALTER TABLE … EXECUTE optimize` reports nothing about what it did,
so these are measured by the runner from the table's own `$files` and
`$snapshots` metadata tables on either side of the operations. `None` means
the measurement itself failed — never zero, which would read as "nothing to
reclaim".

layout.description:
The table's full physical layout as the run LEFT it, which is what the
health store is graded on. Absent for a skipped table (nothing was
measured) and for a report from a runner that predates the field, so an
older image degrades to "health is not refreshed by runs" rather than to
a wall of blank measurements.

Opaque in the OpenAPI on purpose: it is transport from the runner into
the health store, and nothing in the console reads it off a run. The
typed shape the UI does read is `IcebergTableHealth`, from the health
routes.

skip_reason.description:
Why the table was skipped (unchanged since last run, out of time budget,
excluded by pattern).

snapshot_id.description:
Snapshot id current at the end of the table's run — the value the next
run compares against when `skip_unchanged` is on.

Org.description: An organization is a collection of [Users](super::user::User) and [DataDocks](super::datadock::DataDock)

dedicated_harbor_namespaces.description:
ADR-0031 (namespace-per-harbor) placement flag, as stored on the org
row. `false` keeps every harbor of this org on the legacy shared
`hf-{org}` namespace; `true` makes newly created harbors receive a
dedicated `hf-{org}-{harbor}` namespace. New orgs are created with
`true` (see `OrganizationsRepository::create_organization`); the
`false` here is only the *deserialization* fallback, and it is
load-bearing deploy-skew safety: an `Org` serialized by an old console
without this field must deserialize to `false` (the legacy path), never
be assumed dedicated.

external_s3_endpoint.description:
External HTTPS S3/RGW endpoint for this org's shared object storage,
set by the operator's OrgStorage reconciler once it is exposed
(`https://<slug>.s3.<domain>`). `None` until provisioned.

logs_retention_days.description:
Per-organization logs retention, in days (ADR-0020). A query-time
visibility clamp: the console never surfaces logs older than this to the
org's members. `None` = no org-specific clamp (the org sees the full
global window). When set, the valid range is `1..=30` (the global
vlsingle disk retention, which stays global regardless of this setting).

OrgFeature.description:
The per-org sellable feature entitlements.

Every variant maps 1:1 onto a [`ConsoleConfigFeatureFlag`] variant — the
deployment-wide Helm flag stays the kill switch and the org entitlement
decides within it (`effective = global AND org`). Deployment-posture flags
(`ShowMarketing`, `ShowDemoBanner`, `VaubanPreview`) deliberately have no
counterpart here: they are unauthenticated-bootstrap state, not
entitlements.

conditions.description:
Full set of `.status.conditions` from the OrgStorage CRD, surfaced
to the UI so operators can see per-subsystem state
(CephObjectStore, OPA, organization, STS role).

OrgUserAttributesResponse.description: Response for organization-wide user attributes (grouped by user).

users.description: Map of user_id to their attributes.

OrganizationInvitation.description:
An invitation row as returned to API callers.

The token itself is deliberately absent: only its SHA-256 hash is persisted
(`token_hash`), and the raw token is delivered to the invitee by email. This
keeps the org-viewer-gated list endpoint from ever exposing a usable token.

invited_by.description:
`None` for owner-bootstrap invitations sent by the platform backoffice,
whose admins are not console users.

OrganizationOverviewResponse.description:
Per-service resource overview for an organization's home page.

One indexed `COUNT(*)` (plus the distinct harbor slugs) per service in a
single query, plus a K8s list for model servings (no DB table), so the home
page loads its deployed-services grid in one request. Each card links into a
harbor that actually holds the resource (see [`ResourceOverviewResponse`]).

OrganizationPolicy.description:
An org-global authorization guardrail (the restrictive counterpart to a
per-principal [`Grant`]). For any request matching `(action, resource)`,
access is denied unless every requirement holds — evaluated for *all*
principals, ANDed into the decision after the identity allow/deny pass.

requirements.description: All must hold for access; otherwise the guardrail denies.

resource_id.description:
Resource id pattern within `resource_type` (exact / ancestor folder /
`*`-suffixed wildcard, e.g. `prod/asia/*`).

resource_uuid.description:
Two-tier key — see `Grant::resource_uuid`. `Some` = attached (the
bucket-policy analogue, immune to slug-reuse snap-back); `None` = the
org-global SCP pattern.

ParsedAttributeResponse.description: Parsed attribute with separate namespace and value.

PartitionInput.description: A compute partition (one Slinky NodeSet + Slurm partition).

default.description: Whether this is the cluster's default partition.

gpu.description: GPUs per compute node. Omit for CPU-only partitions.

name.description: Partition name (DNS-1123 label, unique within the dock).

node_max.description: Maximum compute nodes (also the partition `MaxNodes` cap).

walltime_max.description: Maximum wall-clock time for a job (Slurm `MaxTime`, e.g. `"04:00:00"`).

description.description: Optional description (DB-only, not stored in the CRD).

runtime_image.description: Override the platform Airflow runtime image.

sleep_mode.description: Sleep mode: scale all components to 0.

tags.description: User-defined tags (DB-only, not stored in the CRD).

PatchAppInstanceRequestBody.description:
PATCH body for updating an app instance's DB-only metadata. Does NOT touch
the CRD — use `PATCH .../crd` for spec changes (parameters).

description.description: Optional free-text description. Pass `null` to clear an existing description.

tags.description: Replacement tag list. Pass an empty array to clear all tags.

retention_days.description: Days of backups and WAL archives to keep before expiring them, 1..=35.

description.description: Optional description (DB-only, not stored in CRD).

enabled.description: Suspend (`false`) or resume (`true`) the cluster. `None` leaves it as-is.

home_size.description: Replace the shared `/home` size (K8s `Quantity`). `None` leaves it as-is.

partitions.description:
Replace the partition set (full replace). `None` leaves it as-is; an
empty array is rejected — a dock must keep at least one partition.

Note: dropping a name does NOT delete its NodeSet — the compute nodes
keep running (and billing) until the operator prunes the now-
unreferenced NodeSet on its own schedule. The response's
`orphaned_partitions` lists every name this call dropped so the caller
never mistakes "removed from spec" for "torn down".

tags.description: User-defined tags (DB-only, not stored in CRD).

version.description: Replace the Slinky image tag. `None` leaves it as-is.

orphaned_partitions.description:
Partition names this patch dropped from `spec.slurm.partitions` that
are STILL RUNNING nodes (and still billing): a `partitions` full
replace only stops the operator from referencing a name going
forward, it does not delete the NodeSet. The operator prunes the
orphaned NodeSet on its own reconcile schedule; a name here stops
appearing once that teardown lands (a subsequent `GET` also drops it
from the live `partitions` status). Always empty when this patch left
`partitions` untouched.

clear_health_check.description:
When `true`, removes any existing health check from the spec. Mutually
exclusive with `health_check_path` / `health_check_port`: sending both
returns a 400 Bad Request.

custom_domains.description:
Custom domains to expose the app on. PATCH semantics: `null` (omit)
leaves existing entries alone; an empty array clears them; a non-empty
array replaces the full list.

expose_to_internet.description:
When set, flips internet exposure on or off. `false` removes the platform
host route and all custom-domain routes while keeping the ClusterIP Service.
`true` restores them. Omit to leave the current value unchanged.

file_mounts.description:
Files to mount into the container. PATCH semantics: `null` (omit) leaves
existing entries alone; an empty array clears them; a non-empty array
replaces the full list. Subject to the same per-file and total inline
size caps as `POST`.

image_pull_secrets.description: Names of secrets from the secret store to use as image pull secrets. Replaces existing pull secrets when set.

persistence.description:
Persistent volumes attached to the container. PATCH semantics: `null`
(omit) leaves existing entries alone; an empty array removes every
entry from the spec; a non-empty array replaces the full list.

Note: removing an entry does NOT delete the underlying PVC. The
operator surfaces `PersistenceReady=False` (`OrphanPersistenceVolumes`)
listing the now-unreferenced PVCs and leaves them intact so data is
never lost by accident. The only way to release the volumes is to
delete the `ContainerApp` itself, at which point owner-reference GC
releases the underlying PVs per the StorageClass `reclaimPolicy`.

`size` and `storageClass` are immutable per entry —
the operator surfaces `PersistenceReady=False` (`ImmutablePersistenceChanged`)
and refuses to apply the workload until the change is reverted. Adding
or removing entries is allowed (subject to the orphan behavior above).

port.description:
**Deprecated — use `ports`.** Ignored by the operator once the spec
carries a non-empty `ports`.

ports.description:
Ports the container listens on. PATCH semantics: `null` (omit) leaves
existing entries alone; an empty array clears them, falling back to the
deprecated single `port`; a non-empty array replaces the full list.

resource_version.description:
If set, the patch will be rejected with 409 Conflict when the live object's
resourceVersion differs. Recommended for any UI-driven edit to prevent
silent last-write-wins on concurrent modifications.

PatchContainerAppRequestBody.description:
PATCH body for updating a container app's display metadata.

All fields are optional; omitting a field leaves the stored value unchanged.
To explicitly clear `description`, pass `"description": null`.

description.description: Optional free-text description. Pass `null` to clear an existing description.

name.description: Human-readable display name. Must not be empty when provided.

tags.description: Replacement tag list. Pass an empty array to clear all tags.

code_location_image.description: Image of the user-code (code location) gRPC server.

description.description: Optional description (DB-only, not stored in the CRD).

sleep_mode.description: Sleep mode: scale webserver + daemon to 0.

tags.description: User-defined tags (DB-only, not stored in the CRD).

freeze_writes.description: Toggle write freeze. Reads stay unaffected.

quota_gb.description: New per-bucket quota in GB. `Some(0)` clears the quota (admins only).

New per-tenant storage quota in GB. Enforced by RGW on the tenant
owner. Omit to leave the quota unchanged.

description.description: Optional description (DB-only, not in CRD).

backup_target_id.description:
Attach or change the backup target (by id). Enables on-demand backups on a
previously target-less database. `None` leaves the current target unchanged.

description.description: Optional description (DB-only, not stored in CRD)

expose_to_internet.description:
When false, no external NodePort Service is created and no public endpoint
is published. Flippable after creation.

tags.description: User-defined tags (DB-only, not stored in CRD)

description.description: Optional description (DB-only).

enabled.description:
Start (`true`) or stop (`false`) the workload (#3712).

Stopping releases the GPUs and keeps the resource listed, inspectable
and deletable. Starting re-runs the FULL admission preflight — a
workload the platform stopped for going over budget cannot be started
back into that state by flipping a flag.

default_per_bucket_quota_gb.description: New default per-bucket quota in GB. Applied to *new* buckets.

freeze_writes.description:
Org-wide kill switch. `true` denies all mutating S3 ops across the org
until flipped back. Reads stay unaffected.

storage_quota_gb.description: Org-wide soft cap in GB. Advisory; sum-of-tenant quotas should fit.

PendingPermission.description:
One opencode permission request that is CURRENTLY pending (awaiting a user
decision), normalized into the same `{ id, sessionId, action, resources }`
shape the frontend already derives from the live `permission.asked` event
stream. The list endpoint returns ALL pending requests across ALL sessions
of the workstation (parent + `task` sub-agents) so the browser can reconcile
prompts it never saw on the socket (reconnect, connection gap) and so a
prompt is never lost.

id.description:
Opencode permission request id (`per_...`); reply via the existing
`.../permissions/{rid}/reply` route.

resources.description:
Human-readable subjects of the request: the request's `patterns` when
present, else the single command / filepath from `metadata`, else empty.

session_id.description:
Opencode session id (`ses_...`) the request belongs to — parent or a
`task` sub-agent's child session.

PendingQuestion.description:
One opencode question request that is CURRENTLY pending (awaiting the
user's answers), normalized like `PendingPermission`. The list endpoint
returns ALL pending requests across ALL sessions of the workstation so the
browser can reconcile prompts it never saw on the socket.

call_id.description:
The asking tool call's id (`call_...`); matches the message part's
`call_id` so the UI can render the prompt inline in the thread.

id.description:
Opencode question request id (`que_...`); reply via the
`.../questions/{rid}/reply` route.

message_id.description:
Message the asking `question` tool call belongs to (`msg_...`), when
opencode linked the request to a tool call.

questions.description: The questions to put to the user, in order.

session_id.description: Opencode session id (`ses_...`) the request belongs to.

PermissionAction.description:
The standing permission policy for a tool, as opencode evaluates it before
each invocation. `ask` prompts the user (surfaced as a `PendingPermission`),
`allow` runs silently, `deny` blocks the call outright.

PermissionCatalogEntry.description: A row of the permission catalog, as exposed to the management UI.

PermissionLevel.description: Permission level granted to the Postgres role.

PermissionPolicyView.description:
The current standing permission policy of a workstation's opencode agent,
read from `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` via opencode's own config API.

allow_all.description:
True when the global policy is the bare string `"allow"` — every tool
runs without a prompt. When true, `tools` is empty.

tools.description:
Per-tool actions for the known tool set, sorted by tool name. Empty when
`allow_all` is true.

PermissionReply.description:
How the user answered an opencode permission prompt. Mirrors opencode's
reply endpoint contract: `once` allows this single invocation, `always`
allows future invocations of the same action, `reject` denies it. Invalid
values are rejected at deserialize time so the BFF never forwards garbage.

message.description: Optional human note forwarded to opencode (e.g. a reject reason).

PersistenceInput.description:
One persistent volume attached to the container.

Lifecycle is coupled to the `ContainerApp` — deleting the app deletes the
PVC, which in turn releases the PV per its StorageClass `reclaimPolicy`.
PVCs are always `ReadWriteOnce`; `size` and `storageClass` are immutable
after creation (volume expansion is out of scope for v1).

mount_path.description: Absolute filesystem path inside the container, e.g. `/data`.

name.description:
Logical name within the `ContainerApp`. Must be a DNS-1123 label
fragment (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; 1-50 chars; cannot start
or end with a hyphen).

storage_class.description: StorageClass name. When omitted, the cluster default is used.

PersistenceResponse.description: One persistent volume attached to the container, as returned to the UI.

PipelineDetailField.description:
A single labeled field shown on a connector detail page.
Sensitive fields are masked in the UI; copyable fields show a copy button.

PipelineDetailGroup.description:
One section of a pipeline's configuration — its connections, or one step.

Grouped rather than flat because the flat form had to carry the structure in
every label ("Labelize · Api key"), repeating the step name down the panel
and leaving the reader to spot where one step ended and the next began.

description.description: What the step does, where the spec says so.

step_type.description:
The executor step type this section describes, e.g.
`hyperfluid.builtins.labelize`. Passed through rather than translated:
naming and iconography for a step belong to the console, which owns the
graph vocabulary the reader has just seen above. Absent for the
connections section, and for a step whose spec omits its type.

title.description: The step's name, or the heading for the pipeline's connections.

destination_prefix.description:
The destination prefix applied to all files written to the destination bucket.
Used to construct the correct S3 browser path from a source-relative ref key.

harbor_id.description:
Harbor the pipeline is placed in, or `null` for a pipeline that is not
assigned to one and therefore runs in the org-wide namespace.

schedule.description: Cron expression for scheduled pipelines, or "one_off" for one-time runs.

oneOf.description: An object-storage bucket, by name — which is how its page is addressed.
A model served by the LLM Gateway, by catalog name.
One Iceberg table, in the data container its catalog belongs to.

PipelineFieldReference.description:
The Hyperfluid resource a detail field's value refers to, so the console can
