link to it instead of printing a dead string.

Resolved on this side rather than by sniffing the rendered value: the console
would otherwise have to re-derive from a display string (`s3://bucket/prefix`,
`catalog.schema.table`) what is known exactly here, and would follow the
wrong link the first time a rendering changed.

Every variant carries what the console's route needs, already resolved — a
table names its data container by id, because that is what the catalog page
is addressed by, even though the executor spec only ever names its catalog.

dc_bucket_id.description: UUID of the bucket Data Container (not required for Copy pipeline)

dd_source.description: UUID of the source object storage Data Dock (not required for Copy pipeline)

import_api_extra_filter_field.description: Copy pipeline: optional extra field filter key (e.g. "rubrique_parent_title")

import_api_extra_filter_value.description: Copy pipeline: optional extra field filter value

routing_rules.description:
FileRouter routing rules: label -> list of destinations
Example: {"type::invoice": [DestinationConfig { data_dock_id: "uuid", bucket_id: "uuid", prefix: "invoices/" }]}

PipelineMetadata.description: Pipeline metadata configuration (common to all pipeline types)

enabled.description:
Whether the pipeline is enabled. A disabled pipeline is created
suspended and runs nothing until it is resumed.

harbor_id.description:
Harbor the pipeline belongs to.

Omit it for org-wide placement in `pp-{organization_id}`, which is what
every legacy pipeline uses and what a `pipelines` row with
`harbor_id IS NULL` resolves to.

max_duration_minutes.description:
Wall-clock budget for one run, in minutes (1..=1440).

Omit it — the default — to let the run's budget follow its own cadence:
three times the schedule's interval, clamped into 15 minutes ..= 6 hours.
Set it for the run that genuinely needs longer than its cadence suggests,
such as a bulk ingest on a tight polling schedule.

name.description: Pipeline name

schedule.description:
Cron expression (5-field) or "one_off" for a one-time run.

Omit it to get the pipeline type's own default cadence — every ten
minutes for most, every six hours for the context enricher — which is
the value each of them used to apply. Send `"one_off"` explicitly to ask
for a single run.

trigger_immediate_run.description:
When true, spawn an immediate Job in addition to the CronJob on creation.
Only meaningful for scheduled (non-one_off), enabled pipelines.

oneOf.description: FileSorter: HephaistosPdfeed + Labelize + CategoryRouterMetadataAware
Copy: Import from external API to S3 destination

enabled.description:
Whether the pipeline is enabled. A disabled pipeline is created
suspended and runs nothing until it is resumed. Defaults to true.

schedule.description:
Cron expression (5-field) or "one_off" for a one-time run.

Omit it for a single run — the V1 API's historical default.

trigger_immediate_run.description: When true, spawn an immediate Job in addition to the CronJob on creation.

harbor_id.description:
Harbor the pipeline is placed in, or `null` for a pipeline that is not
assigned to one and therefore runs in the org-wide namespace.

status.description:
`true` while the pipeline is scheduling runs — the inverse of
[`Self::suspended`], kept as the field older clients read.

suspended.description:
Whether the underlying CronJob is suspended (no new scheduled runs).
Read from the pipeline CRD, so it reflects what the cluster will do
rather than what the console last asked for.

pod_name.description:
Name of the pod that executed the run, reported by the executor via the
downward API. Scopes the run's log query to that pod's collected stream
(ADR-0020); `None` falls back to the console-written stream.

PipelineStats.description: Aggregated statistics for a pipeline, derived from its run history.

PipelineStatusFilter.description:
Server-side status filter for `GET .../pipelines`, over the `suspended`
column (persisted from the CRD — see the `pipelines.suspended` migration).

PipelineTypeCount.description:
One pipeline type's share of the organization's pipelines, for the "types
in use" breakdown on the pipelines overview page.

count.description: Pipelines of this type, in the organization.

PipelinesPage.description:
One page of `GET /organizations/{organization_id}/pipelines`.

Shape mirrors `ManagedPostgresqlBackupsPage` (`data`/`total`/`page`/`limit`) —
same pagination contract, different resource.

total.description:
Total rows matching the filters, ignoring `page`/`limit` — for the
caller to compute page count.

PipelinesStats.description:
Response for `GET /organizations/{organization_id}/pipelines/stats` — every
number the pipelines overview page needs, aggregated in SQL rather than
derived client-side from a fetched page of rows (which silently undercounts
past the list endpoint's page-size ceiling).

by_type.description: Per-type counts, most common type first.

recent.description:
The most recently created pipelines, newest first. Capped at 6 to match
`RECENT_LIMIT` in the console's `pipelines/overview.tsx`.

suspended.description: Pipelines with no new scheduled runs (`suspended = true`).

total.description:
Total pipelines matching the request's scope, across every type and
suspend state.

Platform.description:
An OS/architecture pair. Shared with the registry read views
([`TagResponse`](crate::hf_console::inbound::http::handlers::registry_views::TagResponse)`::platforms`)
— a single `Platform` DTO rather than a second one per consumer.

PolicyPreset.description:
A named, one-click permission policy. `Default` mirrors the workstation's
provisioned policy (write-class → ask, read-class → allow); `AllowAll` is the
live equivalent of `WS_OPENCODE_AUTOAPPROVE` (skip every prompt); `ReadOnly`
denies all write-class tools while keeping reads silent. `Custom` is reported
(never sent) when the live per-tool policy matches none of the presets.

PortProtocol.description: L4 protocol of a `ContainerApp` port, mapping 1:1 to `ServicePort.protocol`.

agent.description:
opencode agent/mode to run this turn under (e.g. "build" or "plan").
Omitted → opencode uses the session default.

attachments.description:
Images attached to the turn (pasted / dropped / picked in the composer).
Each becomes a `data:` URL `file` part next to the text part. `content`
may be empty when at least one attachment is present.

content.description: Raw user content; the BFF wraps it in the opencode message envelope.

model.description:
Model to run this turn on, as "providerID/modelID" (e.g.
"openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet"). Split on the FIRST slash.
Omitted → opencode uses the workstation default model.

PostgresqlConnectorDetail.description:
Detail view of a PostgreSQL connector with the linked DBaaS context
resolved (cluster + user), as served to the catalog detail page.

permission_level.description: Permission level of the linked user (always `viewer` for non-legacy rows).

username.description: Username of the linked managed PostgreSQL user.

PrChecks.description: Rolled-up CI status for a PR, derived from GitHub's `statusCheckRollup`.

branch.description: Branch the changes were pushed to.

number.description:
PR number, parsed from the URL (`…/pull/{number}`, `…/pulls/{number}`, or
`…/-/merge_requests/{number}`, which on GitLab is the per-project `iid`).
`None` when the forge answered with a URL in an unexpected shape.

state.description:
PR state at creation time. Always `OPEN` for a freshly created PR; the
live state is fetched separately via the PR list.

url.description:
Web URL of the pull request the pod opened, or of the merge request on
GitLab.

from_workstation.description:
Whether this PR was opened from a Hyperfluid workstation (branch prefix
`hf/`), so the UI can surface "your" PRs first.

state.description:
`OPEN`, `MERGED`, or `CLOSED`: GitHub's uppercase state, which the other
providers' arms map onto so the UI reads one vocabulary. A GitLab merge
request GitLab is merging right now (`locked`) reports `OPEN`.

destination_bucket_name.description: Staging bucket the archive object is uploaded to (same Harbor).

destination_file_name.description: The name of the archive file.

destination_file_path.description: Optional path prefix within the staging bucket.

file_size.description: The size of the file in bytes — determines the upload strategy.

oneOf.description: Simple single PUT upload for files below the multipart threshold.
Multipart upload for large files.

PreviewPort.description:
One previewable port. `declared` and `detected` are independent: a declared
port with nothing listening is still offered (the user may be about to start
the dev server), and a detected port nobody declared is offered too.

detected.description:
Answering HTTP inside the pod right now, per `hf-ws-daemon`. Always
`false` when the daemon is unreachable — the console cannot tell "not
listening" from "cannot ask".

PreviewPortsResponse.description:
Declared ports first, in their configured order, then detected-only ports
ascending. The picker defaults to the first entry, so this ordering is part
of the contract.

PrincipalUsage.description:
Token totals grouped by principal. `principal_type` is `"api_key"` |
`"service_account"` | `"user"` | `"unknown"`; `principal_id` is the
principal's console DB row id (or `"unknown"`). `name` is `None` for the
unknown sentinel or a principal that has since been deleted; `key_prefix` is
populated for API-key principals only.

PrincipalUsageTimePoint.description:
One point of the consumption-over-time series, for a single principal.

Bucket geometry matches [`ModelUsageTimePoint`]. The principal fields carry
the same identity and name-resolution semantics as [`PrincipalUsage`]:
`name` is `None` for the unknown sentinel or a since-deleted principal, and
`key_prefix` is populated for API keys only.

PropertyDefinition.description:
A typed attribute of an Object Type, optionally mapped to a physical
column of the backing table. `data_type` is a free-form semantic type
(string/integer/double/boolean/date/timestamp/geo/array/struct/...),
intentionally not a Rust enum — same posture as the migration's own
comment: the vocabulary must evolve without a schema migration.

ProposedLinkType.description:
One proposed [`LinkType`], with its endpoints named by `api_name` (not
`Uuid` — those don't exist yet) so it can only ever reference an object
type present in the same proposal.

cardinality.description:
One of [`LINK_CARDINALITIES`] — re-validated by both
`OntologyCopilotService::generate` and `apply_proposal`; an invalid
value is dropped, never trusted as-is.

ProposedObjectType.description:
One proposed [`ObjectType`], ungrounded (no `id`/`organization_id` — those
only exist once `apply_proposal` persists it).

data_type.description:
One of string|integer|double|boolean|date|timestamp (open-ended like
[`PropertyDefinition::data_type`] — not validated against a closed
set, since the vocabulary is free-form by design).

result_data.description:
The run's actual output — `{columns, rows, total_rows, truncated}` —
populated only for scheduled runs (`scheduled_query_id.is_some()`),
capped to `MAX_STORED_RESULT_ROWS`. `None` on every row returned by
`list()` (kept out of that query to stay light for the interactive
History tab); only a single-entry fetch selects it.

scheduled_query_id.description:
Set when a scheduler triggered this run, to the id of the saved query
whose `schedule` came due — `saved_query_id` alone cannot tell a
scheduled run from a user clicking Run on the same saved query.

Reserved by the original SQL Runner design (PRD-001), which modelled a
scheduled query as its own entity. A schedule is a property of a saved
query instead, so this now points at that saved query rather than at a
separate row. Populated whenever a run is schedule-triggered — the
cron poller or an on-demand `run_saved_query` call — and `None` for
ordinary interactive runs.

QuestionInfo.description: One question inside a pending question request.

custom.description:
True when a free-text custom answer is allowed (opencode defaults to
allowing it when the field is absent).

header.description: Very short label (chip/tag) for the question.

multiple.description: True when several options may be selected.

question.description: The complete question to ask the user.

QuestionOption.description: One selectable choice of a question.

description.description: Explanation of what choosing this option means.

QuotaCapacityDimension.description:
The dimensions that can be capacity-constrained.

Profile limits use integer columns (`max_vcpu` cores, `max_ram_gb` GiB,
`max_storage_gb` GiB, `max_gpus` devices). [`QuotaProfile::capacity_limit`]
converts them to the canonical units used throughout the enforcement path.

Not every dimension is measured the same way, and that difference is
load-bearing — see [`QuotaCapacityDimension::COMPUTE`].

max_gpus.description: GPUs the org may hold at once, across every workload kind (#3708).

max_llm_rpm.description:
Inference requests per minute allowed through the LLM gateway
(ADR-0039). `-1` = unlimited, in which case the platform's
`InferencePolicy` defaults apply instead.

max_llm_tpm.description: Inference tokens per minute, same contract as `max_llm_rpm`.

Ref.description:
A reference to a file in a storage bucket
This reference is created upon scanning a bucket and is used to track the
status of the file through the pipeline.

labels.description:
ARN-style metadata accumulated per step for this ref. Append-only.
Format `hf:pipelines:{kind}[:{qualifier}]::{value}` — see
`crate::models::labels` for builders. Used by retriable steps to skip
already-completed work and by routing steps to record produced paths.

locked_by.description:
The ID of the pipeline run that locked the reference
This is used to track the progress of the pipeline run
If the pipeline run is unhealthy (missed a heartbeat), the reference
will be unlocked and the pipeline run will be considered failed.

RefreshCredentialsSummary.description:
Summary returned by `PipelineCrdPublisher::refresh_pipeline_credentials`.
Lists which backing source (`legacy` per-DataDock Vault, `shared_rgw` per-Org
RGW) supplied creds for each S3 connection that was rewritten.

sources.description:
Backing source per refreshed S3 connection. Values are `"legacy"` or
`"shared_rgw"`. Duplicates are kept so callers can see one entry per
connection that was patched.

RegisterOptimizeRunRequest.description:
The runner claiming a run before it starts working.

`run_id` is present for a manual trigger (the console created the row so the
UI could show it immediately) and absent for a scheduled one, where the row
is created here — which is why a cron run appears in the history at all.

RegisterOptimizeRunResponse.description:
What the runner needs back to do its job: which run it owns, and the
snapshot each table was left at by the last successful run (the
`skip_unchanged` comparison basis).

previous_snapshots.description:
Fully qualified table name (`catalog.schema.table`, exactly as the run
reports it in `table_results`) → the snapshot id the last successful run
left it at. Empty when `skip_unchanged` is off or no run has succeeded
yet.

RegistryProjectUsageResponse.description: Per-project usage rollup within the registry (counts + best-effort size).

approximate_size_bytes.description:
Best-effort sum of manifest sizes (`config + layers`) across this
project's tags, in bytes. **Approximate** — see
[`byte_usage_pending`](RegistryUsageResponse::byte_usage_pending).

repository_count.description: Number of repositories under this project (the caller can pull from).

tag_count.description: Total number of tags across this project's repositories.

RegistryResponse.description:
The `registries` row returned by both the internal (operator) and external
(UI) registry routes. Defined once here to avoid the `RegistryResponse` /
`RegistryCrdResponse` split that previously existed across the bridge and
external create handlers — both structs had identical fields and identical
`From<domain::Registry>` impls.

`is_ready` and `external_endpoint` are operator-synced status fields
(persisted via the internal `update_registry_status` endpoint). External
read handlers (list, get) serve these from the DB — never from the K8s API
server (CLAUDE.md operator architecture rule).

Referenced in both `InternalRegistriesApi` and `ExternalRegistriesApi`
OpenAPI component schemas; utoipa deduplicates by schema name so the single
`RegistryResponse` definition is emitted once in each generated spec.

external_endpoint.description:
The external registry host once the reconciler reconciles the
Gateway/HTTPRoute — the per-org subdomain `<org>.rg.<base-domain>`
(ADR-0014 §Scoping amendment). `None` until ready.

harbor_id.description: Harbor that owns this registry (one-per-harbor, ADR-0014 §Scoping).

RegistryRole.description:
A member's role within the registry org (ADR-0014 frozen contract).

The DB stores this as the `registry_role` Postgres enum; the Rust mapping
follows the prevailing `secret_type` pattern (`sqlx::Type` +
`#[sqlx(type_name = ...)]`).

**Role → registry-scope mapping (v1)** — see [`RegistryRole::scopes`]:
`viewer` → `pull`; `editor`/`owner` → `pull,push,delete`. `editor` ≡ `owner`
in v1, kept distinct in the enum for later tightening (no data migration when
they diverge). `manage` is a console-API capability, NOT a registry scope.

RegistryTokenResponse.description: Docker token-auth success body (returned by the real impl in #2294).

RegistryUsageResponse.description:
The per-harbor registry usage / quota read model (ADR-0014 #2303).

Returns the **exact per-harbor quota limit** (from the Registry CR
`spec.storage_quota_gb`; `null` ⇒ inherits the org `OrgStorage` quota), plus
repository / tag **counts** and a **best-effort** size sum derived from the
manifests the caller can pull. **Byte-level per-project usage accounting is
DEFERRED to #2300** (push-time blob accounting in the broker); until then
`byte_usage_pending = true` flags every size field as approximate and not
authoritative — the UI (#2307) must label it as such.

approximate_size_bytes.description:
Best-effort total size in bytes (`Σ config + layers` over visible tags).
**Approximate** — see `byte_usage_pending`.

byte_usage_pending.description:
`true` in v1: byte-level usage is best-effort (summed from manifests the
caller can see, blobs double-counted across projects à la Harbor) and
**authoritative per-project byte accounting is pending #2300**. The UI
must surface size as approximate while this is `true`.

quota_limit_gb.description:
Per-org storage quota in GB (exact, via the Ceph tenant `max_size`).
`null` means the registry inherits the org's `OrgStorage` quota (the
effective limit is resolved by the operator and not on the CR spec).

repository_count.description: Total repositories the caller can see (all projects, gated by org role).

name.description:
New tmux session name. Must match the same charset as creation
(`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, max 64); the server re-sanitizes regardless.

RequestedSize.description:
The trial tier requested on the public form; maps to the `trial-s` /
`trial-m` quota profiles (`quota_profile_slug`), prefilled as the default
in the admin approve dialog.

RequesterKind.description:
Who is requesting a trial (public signup form). Stored as the matching
lowercase/snake_case string in `signup_requests.requester_kind` (see the
table's CHECK constraint) — `as_str`/`parse_str` are the single source of
truth for that mapping.

ResolvedGrant.description:
One fully-resolved effective permission for a principal: a permission the
principal can exercise — directly, expanded from a role bundle, or inherited
through a group — together with the scope it applies at and its effect. This
is the exact projection the OPA enforcement reads, filtered to one subject,
so the "resolved access" preview can never drift from what is enforced.

conditional.description:
`true` when the grant carries a principal-attribute condition, so the
effective access is conditional rather than unconditional.

resource_id.description:
Scope key within the family (a harbor slug, a folder path, or a `*`
wildcard); `None` with `resource_type` = organization-wide.

resource_type.description: Resource family the scope targets; `None` = organization-wide.

ResourceDenialCount.description: Count of denials for a resource.

ResourceFamily.description: One node of the resource hierarchy: a family and the family it nests under.

parent.description:
The family this one nests under (ancestor grants cascade down), or `null`
for a root / org-scoped family.

ResourceKind.description:
Which monitoring target family a rule watches. One variant per
`MonitoringTarget`, because that is what decides how `resource_ref` is
resolved into a live target at evaluation time.

## `resource_ref` spellings
Every kind but one stores a single identifier: a resource UUID, or — for
[`ResourceKind::Model`] — the ISVC name (its namespace is derived from the
org itself). [`ResourceKind::GithubRunnerPool`] is the exception and stores
`"{harbor_id}/{pool_name}"`, because a CI Farm pool has no row and no id of
its own: it is keyed by the harbor that owns it plus its `metadata.name`,
and the pool name alone is not unique across an org's harbors.

histogram.description:
Volume-over-time histogram buckets, ascending by time — for the bar
chart above the entries. Reflects the active search/level/pod/container
filters and the query window. Best-effort: empty when the facet query
returned nothing or failed.

limit.description: Effective (clamped) entry cap applied to this query.

sources.description:
Distinct (pod, container) sources present in scope, most active first —
for the UI source filter. Best-effort: empty when the facet query
returned nothing or failed.

truncated.description:
True when the backend returned `limit` entries — older matching
entries likely exist beyond the cap.

ResourceMode.description:
Governs what happens with the CPU rightsizing recommendation (#3635)
computed for this app every 6h from its measured p95 CPU usage.

This is a display/action policy read by the console — the operator never
reads it, and it changes nothing about what gets rendered into the
Deployment. `workload.resources` (request/limit/entitlement) remains the
only spec the scheduler and the operator act on.

- `Manual` — the recommendation is measured (see
  `container_app_rightsizing_recommendations`) but never surfaced.
- `Advisory` (default) — the console shows a banner with the measured
  value and, for an under-sized app, a one-click path to the next tier;
  the customer decides whether to apply it.
- `Managed` — reserved for #3637 (the platform applies the
  recommendation automatically). Not implemented yet: the console
  currently treats `Managed` the same as `Manual` (no surface) rather
  than pretending to manage something no job acts on.

ResourceOverviewResponse.description:
One line of the org overview: the total across the organization plus the
slugs of the harbors that hold at least one. `harbors` is empty and
`is_org_wide` is `true` for resources that are not harbor-scoped (pipelines,
dashboards, model servings) — their list pages are org-wide, so the home
card links into the currently selected harbor.

harbors.description: Distinct slugs of the harbors holding at least one (empty when org-wide).

is_org_wide.description: `true` for org-wide resources with no harbor association.

ResourceRequirementsSpec.description:
Resource requests and limits for the container.

`limits.cpu` is intentionally omitted from most defaults: an unset CPU limit
avoids CPU throttling (the kernel CFS scheduler throttles containers that
hit their quota even when the node has spare capacity). Set it only when you
need hard isolation guarantees.

ResourceSource.description:
Whether a schema / table was declared via a Hyperfluid CRD
(`TrinoSchema`, `TrinoTable`) or materialized ad-hoc through Trino DDL.

Lives here (domain layer) rather than in the HTTP DTO layer because
both domain models and HTTP responses carry this label.

ResourceSpec.description: CPU / memory quantity for a single resource axis (e.g. "500m", "256Mi").

ResourceTier.description:
Predefined resource tiers for container apps.

A tier sells ONE number — `entitlement_cpu_millis`, what the customer
buys and is billed for (ADR-0012 `requests × replicas`... except since
#3628 the *billed* request is no longer the *scheduled* request: see
below). `request`/`limit`/`bonus` are all DERIVED from it via
[`CaasTierConfig`]'s ratios, never a hand-written per-tier pair:

```text
vCPU sold  =  what the customer picks       ->  quota, invoice
  request  =  reserved_ratio of sold        ->  scheduler, density
  limit    =  max(limit_ratio * sold,
                   limit_floor_millis)      ->  ceiling, burst given away
```

The ratios are PLATFORM configuration ([`CaasTierConfig`]), not code —
they were measured on one cluster (chimera / `hyperfluid.cloud`) and must
not silently apply to every deployment this image ships to. Every method
below that derives request/limit/bonus takes the deployment's
`CaasTierConfig` explicitly rather than reading a hardcoded constant.

Memory limits are always equal to memory requests — RAM does not get the
ceiling's gift (it is incompressible; granting headroom above the
reservation would make the pod evictable under pressure).

ResourceTierCatalogEntry.description:
One row of the tier catalog: everything `ResourceTier::to_resource_requirements`
would put on a new container app's CRD spec, plus the derived bonus,
spelled out for direct display rather than requiring the frontend to
parse `"312m"`-style quantity strings.

bonus_cpu_millis.description:
The free burst given away above the sold envelope
(`cpu_limit_millis - entitlement_cpu_millis`).

cpu_limit_millis.description:
The burst ceiling: `CaasTierConfig::limit_ratio` of
`entitlement_cpu_millis`, floored at `CaasTierConfig::limit_floor_millis`.

cpu_request_millis.description:
What the scheduler actually reserves: `CaasTierConfig::reserved_ratio`
of `entitlement_cpu_millis`.

entitlement_cpu_millis.description: What the customer buys and is billed for (ADR-0012 `× replicas`).

memory.description: Memory request and limit (equal — RAM does not get a burst ceiling).

RestoreFromBackup.description:
Optional restore descriptor: bootstrap the new database from an existing
backup instead of initializing it empty.

backup_id.description:
ID of the `ManagedPostgreSQLBackup` to bootstrap (restore) the new
database from. The backup must be `Completed` and live in the same
harbor as the new database.

also_revoked.description:
Keys the published floor cuts along with this one -- every key for the
same principal at a lower epoch. The floor is a minimum, so it cannot
spare them, and reporting them is the only way the caller learns.

RightsizingDirection.description:
Which way (if any) this app's measured CPU usage diverges from its
current plan — the banner variant for #3636's advisory surface.

RightsizingSuggestionResponse.description:
The CPU rightsizing suggestion for one app (#3635 measures it, #3636
surfaces it). `None` on `ContainerAppCrdSpecResponse` when this app has
never been measured, has fewer than 48h of history, or
`resource_mode != Advisory` — see [`classify_rightsizing`].

entitlement_cpu_millis_at_measurement.description:
The entitlement this app sold at measurement time — what "sized at"
in the over-sized banner refers to. Deliberately the snapshot the
measurement was actually taken against, not the (possibly since
changed) live `entitlement_cpu_millis` above.

measured_at.description: When the #3635 job last measured this app.

p95_cpu_millis.description:
p95 CPU usage over the trailing 7 days, millicores. `None` when the
job ran but the query returned no series.

recommended_reserved_cpu_millis.description:
The #3635 policy's last recommended `reserved_vcpu_millis`. `None`
until 48h of history has cleared the guard for this app.

reservation_cpu_millis_at_measurement.description:
The guaranteed reservation the measurement was classified against —
`ResourceTier::cpu_request_millis` for the tier matching
`entitlement_cpu_millis_at_measurement`, under this deployment's
`CaasTierConfig`. What the under-sized banner's "guaranteed only …"
figure is. `None` when `direction` is `None` (nothing was classified,
so there is nothing this number would explain).

is_generated.description:
`true` when the backing account was auto-generated by the scoped-key flow
(client id `s3key-…`), so it exists only to hold this key's grants and can
be deleted alongside the key. `false` for a customer's own account (the
"for a service account" path) or a key whose account was deleted.

is_platform_managed.description:
`true` when the backing service account is platform-managed (e.g. the
backup/registry/dag-sync identities the platform provisions). Such a key
is shown for audit but is not the customer's to revoke or rotate — that
is the platform's lifecycle. `false` when the account is customer-owned,
or has outlived (its account was deleted).

permissions.description:
Distinct bucket permission keys (e.g. `bucket:read_objects`) granted at
those scopes. Same emptiness rules as `scopes`.

scopes.description:
Distinct bucket-grant `scope_path`s held by the key's backing service
account, at the time of listing. Empty when the key has outlived its
account (there is deliberately no FK from the ledger to
`service_accounts` — see `record_s3_long_lived_key`), or when the
account holds no bucket grants (e.g. an org-wide grant, which is
deliberately excluded — see `list_s3_keys`).

service_account_id.description:
The backing service account's id, so the ledger can rotate the key (mint
a successor for the same account). `None` when the key has outlived its
account, in which case it can be revoked but not rotated.

region.description:
SigV4 signs over the region: ours is the RGW zonegroup `api_name`
(`default`), not `us-east-1`. Wrong value fails every signature check.

SavedQueriesPage.description:
One page of `GET /api/v1/tiny-query/queries`.

Shape mirrors `PipelinesPage` (`data`/`total`/`page`/`limit`) — same
pagination contract, different resource.

total.description:
Total rows matching the filters, ignoring `page`/`limit` — for the
caller to compute page count.

ScanStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an image scan row (DB `scan_status` ENUM). Mirrors the
`registry_role` mapping pattern (`sqlx::Type` + `#[sqlx(type_name = ...)]`).

ScanSummary.description:
Lightweight projection for read-views (catalog/tag badges) and list endpoints
— never carries the full `report` blob.

ScanTrigger.description:
What requested a scan (DB `registry_scan_trigger` ENUM). Mirrors the
`ScanTrigger` carried on the `RegistryScan` CRD (`hf_lib_domain_core`); kept
as a separate console-DB enum so the domain crate takes no console dep.

granted.description:
Whether the caller has a background-execution grant on file — an
existence check only (see `UserAccessTokenBroker::has_grant`), not a
guarantee the refresh token is still accepted by Keycloak.

ScheduleState.description:
A saved query's cron schedule and everything about its scheduled
execution — grouped into one type so "does this query have a schedule"
and "what's its run state" can't drift apart into independently optional
columns that are only ever meaningful together. `None` on
`SavedQuery.schedule` means on-demand execution only; every field here is
otherwise only ever read once that's `Some`.

consecutive_failures.description:
Consecutive scheduled-run failures, reset to 0 on a successful run.
Lets the UI distinguish a single blip from a schedule that's been
failing repeatedly.

cron.description:
Cron expression in the platform's shared dialect — the same grammar
Pipelines accept (5 fields with ranges/steps/lists and `JAN`/`MON`
names, or a `@daily`/`@every 1h` shorthand), validated by
`hf_lib_domain_pipeline::models::validate_schedule`.

Always evaluated in **UTC**, like every other cron on the platform
(Pipeline CronJobs, Iceberg optimize, CNPG scheduled backups). There is
deliberately no per-query timezone: adding one is a product decision
that has to cover DST for all of them at once, not just this surface.

last_error.description:
Why the last run failed. **Redacted to `None` for every reader except
the query's owner** (see `SavedQuery::redact_for`): engine errors
name catalogs, schemas, tables and columns, and any org member can read
any saved query today, so a raw passthrough would route Trino's error
text around the dock's OPA column policy.

last_success_at.description:
When this schedule last completed successfully, distinct from
`last_run_at` (which updates on every attempt, success or failure).
`None` if it has never succeeded. Measures staleness in wall-clock
time — `consecutive_failures` alone can't tell a 5-minute schedule
apart from a daily one that's failed the same number of times.

next_run_at.description:
When the next run is due.

`None` means "due at the next poll" — the scheduler's claim predicate is
`(next_run_at IS NULL OR next_run_at <= now())`, so a freshly created or
freshly re-scheduled query runs on the next tick rather than waiting for
something to compute an occurrence first. Nothing populates this yet;
see the schedule columns in the migration for the intended writer.

suspended.description:
While `true`, the poller's `claim_due` never claims this row, even
past its stored `next_run_at` — a schedule can be paused without
losing its cron or its run history.

ScheduledRunStatus.description:
Outcome of a saved query's most recent scheduled run.

Mirrored into the DB column `last_status` (TEXT with a CHECK constraint on
the same vocabulary) and into the OpenAPI spec as an `enum`, so every
consumer — frontend via hey-api, operator via progenitor, SDK users — sees
the same closed set instead of guessing at free-form text.

ScmBranch.description: A branch the user can pick after settling on a repo.

ScmRepository.description: A repository the user can pick to clone into a dev-workstation.

clone_url.description:
HTTPS clone URL, ready to use as the workstation's `repo_url`. Built
server-side from an origin the console validated — github.com for a
GitHub credential, the credential's own instance for GitLab — because a
self-managed GitLab is only knowable from the credential, and because
this string decides what a workstation fetches and offers its token to.

default_branch.description: Default branch — pre-fills the branch picker as a sensible starting point.

description.description: Short description for the picker subtitle, if the SCM has one.

full_name.description:
Canonical path identifier: `owner/name` on GitHub, and the full
`group/subgroup/project` path on GitLab, where namespaces nest. Pass it
back verbatim as the `repo` parameter of the branches endpoint.

html_url.description:
Browsable URL on the forge the credential points at, behind the picker's
open-in-a-new-tab link.

updated_at.description:
ISO-8601 timestamp of the last push, used to sort and label the picker
rows ("Updated 3 days ago").

prefixes.description:
Object-key prefixes the key is confined to within `bucket`. Empty means
the whole bucket. One grant set is written per prefix.

SearchMode.description:
How to interpret the free-text `search` term (logs explorer).

- `Text` (default): a case-insensitive SUBSTRING match. The term is
  RE2-escaped so every metacharacter is literal — `health` matches
  `GET /healthz`, `a.b` matches only a literal `a.b`.
- `Regex`: the term is a user-authored RE2 pattern, validated to compile
  before it is embedded. Still forced case-insensitive (a power user can
  override with an inline `(?-i)`).

Both modes render to the same `~"(?i)…"` LogsQL regex filter on `_msg`; the
only difference is whether the term is escaped (Text) or passed through
(Regex). The term is always wrapped in a length-capped, quote/backslash
escaped LogsQL string — never raw query syntax.

owner_user_id.description:
Set only for user-scoped secrets: the owning principal's oidc sub, which
is also the second segment of `name` (`users/<owner_user_id>/<leaf>`).

SecretRef.description:
A Passe-Partout secret, addressed the way the secret store addresses one:
`organizations/{organization_id}/{secret_id}`.

Deliberately not `hf_lib_domain_core::dev_workstations::crd::ScmSecretRef`,
which carries the same two fields for the agent's model key: that one is
named for source-control credentials, lives in the workstation module, and
derives neither `PartialEq` nor `ToSchema`, both of which this needs. Kept
structurally identical so the two can be merged if a neutral home appears.

SecretScope.description: Visibility scope of a secret. Immutable after creation.

SecretType.description: The type of value stored in the secret.

SenderPattern.description:
A sender pattern used to filter inbound email by the `From` address.
The pattern is matched case-insensitively as an exact address or domain suffix.

enabled.description: Mirrored from the CRD. `false` means the account cannot obtain new tokens.

iam_sa_client_id.description: The client_id of the Keycloak client.

iam_sa_credentials_path.description: The secret path in the secret store for the service account credentials.

iam_sa_id.description: This is the storage ID of the Keycloak client NOT the client_id.

managed_by_resource_type.description:
[`ResourceType`] key of the owning resource
(`backup_target` | `registry` | `airflow` | `data_dock`), `null` when
customer-owned.

public_client.description:
Mirrored from the `ServiceAccount` CRD by the operator. Kept on the row
so the list screen can show and filter the client type without reading
custom resources.

ServiceAccountCrdConfig.description:
Keycloak-client settings read back from the `ServiceAccount` CRD, for the
console's configuration screen. These live only on the CRD — the console
database row carries identity and credentials, not client settings.

public_client.description:
`true` means a browser-flow (public) client that authenticates without a
secret. Such an account has no downloadable credentials.

ready.description: `true` once the operator has reconciled the spec into Keycloak.

secret_rotation_pending.description: Set while a requested secret rotation has not been applied yet.

ServiceLinkKind.description:
The kind of a service participating in a link. Constrained to the kinds the
ServiceLink controller knows how to resolve into a pod selector + port.

Object storage (shared Ceph/RGW) and the Hyperfluid platform control plane
are deliberately NOT link kinds: both are effectively always-reachable
(object storage is internet-exposed; the platform is a hard runtime
dependency), so their egress lives unconditionally in every workload's
baseline policy rather than being declared per-link (ADR-0021 §6–§7).

ServiceLinkPort.description:
A `(port, protocol)` pair a link opens on its target. `protocol` is the L4
protocol spelled as Kubernetes does — `TCP`, `UDP`, or `SCTP`.

ServiceLinkResponse.description:
A service link as surfaced to the console UI. Built directly from the CRD —
there is no database row (links are pure custom resources).

name.description: The CRD object name (also the link's identifier within a harbor).

ports.description:
The `(port, protocol)` pairs the operator opened for this link; empty
until it has reconciled.

ready.description: Aggregate readiness from the CRD status conditions.

ServiceRef.description:
One endpoint of a link: a service of a known kind, referenced by name within
the harbor namespace the link lives in (both endpoints are co-located).

SessionSummary.description:
A session row for the chat session rail. `title` is whatever opencode
stored at create time — for our sessions that is the agent preset name
(e.g. "Code Helper"), so the rail reads as a list of named conversations
instead of opaque ids.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 created timestamp from opencode's `time.created` (epoch ms).

id.description: Opencode session id (`ses_...`).

parent_id.description:
Parent session id when this is a `task` sub-agent's child session
(opencode's `parentID`). Lets the frontend scope prompts to a session's
family and keep child sessions out of the rail.

title.description: Human title set at create time; empty if opencode had none.

SetApiKeyRateLimitsRequest.description:
Replace this key's tenant-set rate ceilings. Sent whole, never merged: an
absent (or null) axis CLEARS that ceiling, because clearing one is exactly
the operation an admin performs to loosen a limit and a merge patch would
read it as "leave it alone" (the same rule ADR-0039 applies to policies).

channel_ids.description: Channels that receive this signal. Empty = every enabled channel.

SetDedicatedHarborNamespacesRequestBody.description:
Body to enable/disable the org's ADR-0031 "dedicated harbor namespaces"
opt-in. Unlike the nullable settings above, this mirrors the underlying
`NOT NULL bool` column — the caller always states the desired value, there
is no "clear" state.

SetKeyBudgetBody.description:
Set one ceiling on one API key.

Organization-wide ceilings are deliberately NOT settable here: they bound
the platform's exposure and are the cockpit's to set. An org admin
allocates inside what was sold.

credits.description: Whole credits, as a human types them.

SetOrganizationLogsRetentionRequestBody.description:
Body to set an org's per-org logs retention (ADR-0020 query-time visibility
clamp). `null` clears the clamp (the org sees the full global window); a
value must be within `1..=30` days.

SetRolePermissionsRequestBody.description:
Replace a role's whole permission bundle in one request. The role editor
stages adds/removes locally and saves the final set here, so a save is one
round-trip + one projection refresh instead of one per toggle.

permission_ids.description: The complete set of permission ids the role should hold after the save.

SetUserAttributesRequest.description: Request to set all attributes for a user (replaces existing).

attributes.description:
List of attributes in `namespace::value` format.
Example: `["region::occitanie", "department::sales"]`

SetupOutcome.description: Verdict on the LATEST template-setup run of the workstation's pod.

flatten.description: Whether to flatten directory structure (true) or preserve it (false)

length.description: Number of characters from SHA256 hash to use as suffix

active_model.description:
Flavor-only: the highest-weight ready target's shared-model name (the
one shown to users as "active").

context_tokens.description: Flavor-only: the active target's served context window.

gpu.description:
GPU count — one container's limit, so a per-pod figure. Multiply by
`replicas` for what the model occupies cluster-wide.

kind.description:
`"model"` for a raw shared model, `"flavor"` for a platform-owned
`ModelFlavor` binding (ADR-0032). Existing entries carry `kind:
"model"` and `None` for the fields below, so this stays
backward-compatible for callers that don't know about flavors yet.

max_replicas.description:
Autoscaler ceiling (`spec.scaling.maxReplicas`, or a classic
InferenceService's `predictor.maxReplicas`); `null` when the pod count
is fixed.

name.description:
InferenceService name (or external-model name), or a flavor's public
routing name when `kind == "flavor"`

phase.description:
Current phase (Ready, Provisioning, Failed) — or a flavor's phase
(Bound, Degraded, Unbound) when `kind == "flavor"`

replicas.description:
Pods behind the serving: `1` for the ordinary single-pod serving, `0`
for one scaled to zero, the autoscaler's floor when `max_replicas` is
set. `null` when there is no serving to measure — an externally-hosted
model, or a `kind: "flavor"` row, which names a binding rather than a
deployment.

runtime.description:
Inference engine (`vllm`, `sglang`, `tgi`, …), `external` for a model
hosted off-cluster, or `unknown` when the serving's spec names none.

tool_calling.description: Flavor-only: whether the active target advertises tool calling.

public_key.description:
The caller's SSH **public** key in OpenSSH authorized-keys format
(e.g. `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... user@host`). Never a private key.

certificate.description:
The signed OpenSSH user certificate (`ssh-...-cert-v01@openssh.com ...`),
to be written next to the caller's private key as `*-cert.pub`.

principal.description:
The single principal the certificate is valid for — derived from the
authenticated caller, never from the request.

ttl_seconds.description: Certificate lifetime in seconds (3h). The certificate cannot be renewed.

SignalThresholdsDto.description:
One signal's effective thresholds. `*_is_override` tells the UI whether it
is showing a platform default or the org's own value, so "reset to default"
can be offered only when it means something.

signal.description:
`pvc_disk` | `bucket_quota`. `cfs_throttling` never appears here — its
threshold is fixed platform-wide (see `AlertSignal::is_overridable`).

SkillRegistryCatalogEntry.description: One catalog row: everything the picker needs, no skill bodies.

id.description: `null` for a platform registry.

name.description: The value to put in a workstation's `skill_registries[].name`.

SkillRegistryRefDto.description:
A registry a workstation attaches, by name + scope. The wire field on
`DevWorkstation.spec` is snake_case `skill_registries`; this is one element
of it.

name.description:
Registry name (the CR name, and the directory it is mounted at inside the
pod: `/run/skills/<name>`).

SkillRegistryResponse.description: A registry with all of its skills — the editor's payload.

auto_attach.description:
Console policy: the create wizard pre-checks this registry. Always
`false` for a platform registry other than the stock essentials one,
which the wizard pre-checks by name.

id.description: `null` for a platform registry (no DB row; address it by `name`).

name.description:
Slug. Immutable once created: it is the CR name and the in-pod mount
directory, so renaming would move every attached workstation's path.

read_only.description:
`true` for platform registries: they are installed by the chart and no
console call can change them.

revision.description:
Bumped on every mutation; stamped onto the projected CR so the operator
can tell a real change from a re-apply.

root_doc.description:
`REGISTRY.md` — registry-level instructions merged into the agent's
system context.

SkillRegistryScopeDto.description:
Where a registry comes from. Same two values as the CRD's
`WorkstationSkillRegistryScope`, re-declared here because the CRD type is a
`schemars` type and the API surface is a `utoipa` one.

SkillResponse.description:
One skill of a registry, with its markdown body.

`content` is the body **only**: the YAML front matter (including the skill's
`name` and `description`) is composed by the operator when it renders the
file into the workstation, so a body that starts with `---` is rejected on
write.

id.description: `null` for a skill of a platform registry — it has no row.

SkippedPreviewPort.description:
A listening port the daemon deliberately did not offer. Diagnostics for the
UI ("bound to 127.0.0.1 only" / "does not speak HTTP"); never previewable.

reason.description:
`loopback_only` | `not_http` today, free-form by contract: render an
unrecognised value with a default branch rather than assuming a closed
set (a pod keeps the daemon image it was created with).

SpendWindow.description:
What a ceiling is measured over.

Three of the four are rolling. A calendar window lets a caller spend its
whole day in the last minute of one and again in the first minute of the
next, which is exactly the burst a ceiling exists to prevent. `Monthly` is
the calendar month anyway, because that is what an invoice is and a monthly
ceiling that straddles two invoices explains nothing to the person reading
them.

StartHealthScanResponse.description: Result of asking for a sweep.

redirect_path.description:
Where to send the browser back to once the consent redirect
completes, relative to the console's own origin (e.g.
`/harbors/acme/tiny-query`) — the frontend computes this with
`useHarborPath()`, same as any other in-app link. Must be a
same-origin relative path (starts with `/`, not `//`, no `://`, no
`\`), so this endpoint can't be turned into an open redirector.

authorize_url.description: The Keycloak `/auth` URL to redirect the browser to next.

StorageZoneView.description: A `cephZones` catalog entry joined with whether the org has enabled it.

enabled.description: Whether an OrgStorage exists for this org in this zone.

external_endpoint.description: External S3 endpoint of the zone's OrgStorage, once provisioned.

primary.description: The primary zone every org has; always enabled and never removable.

ready.description: Whether the zone's OrgStorage is Ready (only meaningful when enabled).

s3_gateway_enabled.description:
Whether this zone runs an S3 gateway. Off for every org until someone
sets `spec.s3Gateway.enabled`, so the console uses it to hide gateway
affordances rather than offer one that can only 409.

SupportTicketEventResponse.description:
One timeline entry.

On the tenant plane `actor_display` has already been redacted to a generic
label for a platform actor, and assignment rows are absent entirely — both
in SQL, by `list_events_for_tenant`. Which member of the platform team
acted is internal routing, exactly as it is on [`SupportTicketResponse`];
the timeline is the one surface where that could otherwise leak, because
`PlatformAdminIdentity::actor()` is an email address.

SupportTicketMessageResponse.description:
One message in a thread.

There is no `internal_note` field, and that is deliberate: the tenant read
filters internal notes out in SQL, so a flag here could only ever be
`false` — and publishing it would invite a future caller to trust it
instead of the query.

SupportTicketResponse.description:
One ticket as the tenant sees it.

Carries no `assigned_admin_sub`: which member of the platform team owns a
ticket is internal routing, and a customer learning the team's structure
from a ticket payload is a detail nobody asked to publish. The display name
on a reply is all the attribution the thread needs.

reference.description: Human-readable handle, `HF-<n>` — what to quote on a call.

TableHealthFinding.description: One reason a table is not healthy.

observed.description: The measured value. Its unit depends on `kind`; see the variant docs.

remedy.description:
The maintenance operation that fixes it — `compact_files`,
`expire_snapshots`.

threshold.description:
The value `observed` had to cross for this finding to fire, on the same
scale. Returned so the UI can say what the verdict was measured against
instead of asking the reader to trust it.

TableHealthFindingKind.description: The kinds of trouble a layout measurement can reveal.

TableHealthSeverity.description:
How much a table's layout is costing, worst finding first.

`Unknown` is not a middle ground and not a failure — it is the honest answer
for a table whose metadata could not be read. It must never be collapsed
into `Healthy`: "we could not measure this" and "this is fine" are different
claims, and only one of them is safe to act on.

TagResponse.description: One tag with its manifest digest, best-effort size, and platforms.

digest.description:
The manifest content digest (`Docker-Content-Digest`). Empty if the
registry did not return one.

image_created_at.description:
When the image was **built** — the `created` field of its config blob.

Deliberately not called a push time: distribution's v2 API exposes no push
timestamp at all (the tag list returns bare strings and a manifest read
carries no `Last-Modified`), so this builder-stamped instant is the only
time available without persisting registry notification events. For a
CI-built image it tracks the push closely; a retagged or reproducibly
built image can report something much older.

`None` when the config blob could not be read (best-effort), when the
builder omitted `created`, or when it stamped a zero/epoch sentinel.

platforms.description:
The `os`/`architecture` platforms this tag resolves to (Docker-Hub
style). For a multi-arch tag this lists every platform in the index; for
a single-arch tag it is the one platform read off the config blob, or
empty if that best-effort lookup failed. Never fails the tag listing.

size_bytes.description:
Best-effort stored size of the tag in bytes (`config.size + Σ layers[].size`).
For a multi-arch index/manifest-list this is the **sum across platforms**,
deduped by blob digest so a shared layer counts once, with buildx
attestation manifests excluded. A child-manifest fetch failure degrades
that child to `0` — hence best-effort, and marked approximate in the usage
view's `byte_usage_pending`.

TagsResponse.description: Tags for a repository under a project the caller may pull from.

code.description: Stable identifier the frontend can branch on.

message.description: Human-readable detail, mostly for surfacing in the UI.

registry.description: Registry host the request was made against.

tag.description: Tag (or digest) portion of the reference.

image_pull_secret.description: Optional secret-manager entry name with OCI credentials. Omit for public images.

TestImagePullResponse.description:
Result of an interactive image-pull credential test.

The endpoint always returns `200 OK` on a completed test — `ok` discriminates
between a successful manifest probe and a structured registry-side failure.
Surfacing failures as part of a single response shape (rather than a 4xx with
a different body) keeps the generated OpenAPI client typed and lets the UI
branch on `reason` without piggy-backing on HTTP status codes.

ok.description:
`true` when the registry returned a manifest, `false` for any
structured pull failure (auth, not found, tag not found, network, …).

resolved_digest.description:
Manifest digest reported by the registry, e.g. `sha256:…`. Present when
`ok` is `true`.

ok.description:
`true` when the registry validated the credentials or accepted the
request anonymously; `false` for any structured login failure.

TicketCategory.description:
What the ticket is about, chosen by the reporter. Used to route triage, not
to change behaviour.

TicketPriority.description:
How urgent the reporter (or the triaging admin) says it is. Advisory: it
orders the queue, it does not gate anything.

TicketStatus.description:
Where a ticket stands, from the point of view of who owes the next move.

Not settable by a tenant and not settable by an admin except through the
explicit transitions: the value is otherwise derived from who wrote last
(see [`super::service`]). A hand-maintained status column stops describing
anything within a month.

ToolPermission.description:
One tool's standing permission. `tool` is an opencode tool key (e.g. `bash`,
`edit`, `read`).

TopDimension.description:
Grouping dimension for `GET .../bifrost/top` (ADR-0022).

`Tier` is NOT a LogsQL grouping field — Bifrost events carry no
`sensitivity_tier` (classification lives in Console/Vauban, not Bifrost).
The inbound handler serves it by running the `Table` grouping and joining
each table's tier from `table_classifications_service` at read time (see
`handlers::monitoring::bifrost::get_bifrost_top`), which is why the
domain-level [`super::ports::BifrostConsumptionService::top`] method takes
the narrower [`TopGroupBy`] instead of this wire enum.

new_owner_id.description: OIDC user id of the new owner.

TrinoConnectorDescriptorResponse.description: One connector the platform can provision from user-supplied credentials.

connector_kind.description:
The Trino connector id — `mysql`, `postgresql`, … Also the `kind`
string a catalog reports, and the URL segment of its detail page.

docs_url.description:
The documentation page these property names were read off, for the
Trino version actually deployed.

family.description:
Coarse grouping for the connector picker: `jdbc`, `lakehouse`,
`nosql`, `streaming`.

params_schema.description:
JSON Schema of the credential bundle, in the shape the console's
existing schema-driven form renderer consumes: `{properties, required}`
with `title`, `description`, `default` and `format` per property.

`format: "password"` marks a value that must be entered masked and
never rendered back; `format: "textarea"` a multi-line one.

supports_managed_credentials.description:
Whether this connector can also be backed by a Hyperfluid-managed
instance instead of user-supplied credentials. True only for
`postgresql` today (the DBaaS viewer-user path).

The console offers a managed/external choice from this, rather than
from a hardcoded `kind === "Postgresql"`: with the literal, the next
connector added by epic #3559 would open on a "Managed instance" tab
that renders nothing.

dc_iceberg_id.description: UUID of the Iceberg catalog Data Container

dd_trino_int.description: UUID of the Trino Data Dock

model_base_url.description: Base URL for the model API (e.g., vLLM endpoint). Defaults to Mistral API when not set.

UpdateActionTypeRequest.description:
`api_name` and `object_type_id` are deliberately absent — like
[`ObjectType::api_name`] and a link's endpoints, they are the action's
structural identity; retargeting is modelled as delete+recreate.

PATCH semantics are COALESCE-based: an absent/`null` field is left
unchanged, and the nullable `description` cannot be cleared back to
`NULL` via PATCH (`parameters` is not nullable — send `[]` to empty it).

operation.description: One of [`ACTION_OPERATIONS`] when present (validated by the service).

UpdateAiAgentRequest.description:
Partial update. Only present fields are applied. Empty strings clear
`description` / `context` / `inference.model`.

detach_service_account.description: True detaches the current service account.

mission.description: Replaces this capability's own instructions. An empty string clears them.

service_account_id.description: Attach this service account. Ignored when `detach_service_account`.

speciality.description: Replaces the speciality. An empty string clears it.

subagent_of.description: Replaces the owning router. An empty string detaches the subagent.

tools.description: Replaces the tool list. An empty array restores every tool and command.

tables.description:
Allowlist applied when `exposure_mode` is `selected`; ignored (and
cleared) when `all`.

UpdateContextProviderBody.description: Request to update a context provider.

UpdateContextualRestrictionBody.description: Request to update a contextual restriction.

refresh_interval_seconds.description:
Set to `Some(None)` semantics via a sentinel is avoided — send the new
interval, or omit to leave unchanged (issue #2958).

variables.description: Full replacement of the variable list when present (issue #2948).

widgets.description:
Full replacement of the widget list when present (the spec is one
document; partial widget patches are a client-side concern).

UpdateDataDockSecuritySettingsBody.description: Request to update datadock security settings.

UpdateDevWorkstationNetworkRequest.description:
Partial update of a workstation's egress network settings. Every field is
optional; only present fields are applied to the CR `spec.network`.

allowlists.description:
Replaces the workstation's referenced `EgressAllowlist` names when
present. Each must exist in the workstation's harbor namespace.

extra_fqdns.description: Replaces the workstation's extra FQDNs when present.

llm_providers.description: Replaces the workstation's selected managed LLM providers when present.

UpdateDevWorkstationRequest.description:
Partial update of a workstation's inference settings. Every field is
optional; only present fields are applied to the CR `spec.inference`.

inference_model.description:
Provider-qualified opencode model id to default to. When present (even
empty), replaces the workstation's default model; an empty string clears
it so the entrypoint's curated default applies again.

inference_provider.description:
Inference provider: `sapience` (in-cluster LLMaaS), `openrouter`
(external), or `claude` (Claude Code as the workstation agent). When
present, replaces the workstation's provider.

openrouter_key_secret_id.description:
Id of a Passe Partout secret of type `plaintext` holding the OpenRouter
API key. When present, replaces the workstation's key secret reference.

UpdateGithubConnectionRequest.description:
Request body for updating a `GithubConnection`.

Not `Serialize`, for the same reason as [`CreateGithubConnectionRequest`].

The credential is mandatory even when only the host is moving. A stored
credential is write-only — no endpoint hands one back — so there is nothing
to partially edit, and re-proving the replacement against the effective host
is what keeps "I updated the connection" from meaning "my pools start
failing at the next token refresh".

The name is not editable: it is what every pool's `connection_secret_name`
resolves through, so a rename is a delete plus a create, not an update.

base_url.description:
GitHub base URL. Absent keeps the stored host; changing it is refused
while any runner pool still registers against the old one.

UpdateGithubRunnerRequest.description:
Request body for editing a `GithubRunner` pool in place.

**Every field is optional and absent means unchanged** — this is a partial
update, applied to the live CR spec as a JSON merge patch, not a replace.
A field that is present is validated exactly as it would be on create, and
the *merged* result is re-checked against every create-time rule (sizing
ceiling, `min <= max`, image shape, FQDN sanitation, connection exists).

[`scope`](Self::scope) is accepted only so a scope change can be refused
with an explanation: the scope is what the runner scale set is registered
under on GitHub, and moving it means deregistering and re-registering —
delete and recreate the pool instead.

connection.description:
Move the pool to a different `GithubConnection` — the leaf name, same
value `CreateGithubRunnerRequest.connection` takes. Used to swap in a
rotated credential without deregistering the scale set. The new
connection must point at the same GitHub host as the current one.

extra_egress_fqdns.description:
Replacement egress allow-list (it replaces the previous one wholesale,
it is not merged entry by entry). Send `[]` to keep only the built-in
GitHub Actions preset.

max_runners.description: New concurrency ceiling. Live resize, same as `min_runners`.

min_runners.description:
New warm-runner floor. Live resize — ARC changes the target without
recreating pods.

runner_group.description:
New GitHub runner group (org scope only). Send `""` to fall back to
GitHub's default group.

runner_image.description:
New runner container image. Rolls the runner template, same as
`flavor`. Send `""` to go back to the platform-pinned default.

runs_on.description:
New `runs-on:` name. Send `""` to go back to the name Hyperfluid
derives from the pool name.

Unlike every other field here this one is **not** transparent to
running workflows: the scale set is deregistered and registered again
under the new name, so a workflow still saying `runs-on: <old name>`
queues until it is edited.

It is also the only edit with downtime. GitHub will not move a
registration's runner label in place, so the `AutoscalingRunnerSet` is
deleted and re-applied (under its unchanged Kubernetes name). ARC
drains in-flight runners first — no job is killed — but the pool
accepts nothing until the new registration is live. `status.message`
names the old value to keep using meanwhile.

client_secret.description:
Optional on update — when omitted or empty, the secret already stored in
Keycloak is left untouched.

config.description: Whole-map replace when present (not a deep merge).

replicas.description:
Distinguish "field absent" (`None` = keep current value) from "field
set to JSON `null`" (`Some(None)` = clear the override, reverting to
inheriting the service's replication factor) — mirrors
`UpdateKafkaHFServiceRequest`'s `cpu_request`/etc double-Option.

UpdateLinkTypeRequest.description:
The two endpoints (`source_object_type_id`/`target_object_type_id`) are
absent — like `ObjectType::api_name`, they are the link's structural
identity; retargeting a link is modelled as delete+recreate.

PATCH semantics are COALESCE-based: an absent/`null` field is left
unchanged, and the nullable join columns (`source_property`/
`target_property`) cannot be cleared back to `NULL` via PATCH.

UpdateObjectTypeRequest.description:
`api_name` is deliberately absent — see [`ObjectType::api_name`].

PATCH semantics are COALESCE-based: a field that is absent (or `null`) in
the request body is left unchanged, and a nullable column can therefore
NOT be cleared back to `NULL` via PATCH — grounding
(`data_dock_id`/`backing_*`/`primary_key_column`) is effectively one-way
for now (ungrounding would be delete+recreate).

UpdateOrgSecuritySettingsBody.description: Request to update organization security settings.

UpdatePermissionPolicyRequest.description:
Update the standing permission policy. Either pass a `preset` (applied as a
whole, `tools` ignored) or an explicit per-tool `tools` list. `Custom` is not
a valid input preset — send `tools` instead.

tools.description: Explicit per-tool policy. Used when `preset` is absent.

max_duration_minutes.description:
Wall-clock budget for one run, in minutes (1..=1440), or `null` to hand
the budget back to the schedule — three times its interval, clamped into
15 minutes ..= 6 hours.

Applied as stated rather than as a patch, like `suspend` beside it: this
is the value the pipeline should end up with. An omitted field therefore
means "automatic", which is what every pipeline had before the column
existed, so a caller written against the older shape is unaffected.

suspend.description: When true the underlying CronJob is suspended (no new runs will be scheduled).

UpdatePropertyDefinitionRequest.description:
PATCH semantics are COALESCE-based: an absent/`null` field is left
unchanged, and a nullable field (`description`, `source_column`) cannot be
cleared back to `NULL` via PATCH — remapping a property away from a
physical column is delete+recreate for now.

locked_by.description:
Lock-ownership guard: when set, the update only applies if the ref is
still locked by this run. Protects against a run whose refs were
reclaimed (dangling-lock janitor) clobbering the state written by the
run that re-claimed them. When `None` the update is unconditional
(console/manual actions).

schedule.description:
Absent = keep the current schedule; `null` = unschedule the query;
a string = replace the cron.

This is a double option on purpose. With a plain `Option<String>` serde
folds "absent" and "explicit null" together, and the repository's
`.or(current)` fallback then writes the old cron back — which left no
request at all that could stop a scheduled query.

suspended.description:
Omitted leaves suspended state unchanged. `Some(false)` (an explicit
resume) with no schedule text change also recomputes `next_run_at`
fresh from now, rather than firing immediately on a stale, long-past
value.

description.description: `null` clears the description; absent keeps the current value.

UpdateServiceAccountCrdRequestBody.description:
Editable Keycloak-client settings. `client_id` is not among them — the CRD
marks it immutable, since changing it would re-point the account's grants.

public_client.description:
`true` switches the client to browser flow: it authenticates without a
secret, and its stored credentials are dropped.

UpdateSkillRegistryRequest.description:
Patch a harbor registry. Absent fields are untouched; an empty string clears
a nullable one. `name` is absent by design — it is immutable.

description.description: Empty string clears it.

UpdateSkillRequest.description:
Patch a skill. `name` is absent by design — it is immutable (it is the
ConfigMap key and half of the `<registry>--<skill>` identity agents resolve
skills by).

content.description:
Replaces the body when present. Never cleared: a skill with no body is
not a skill.

description.description: Empty string clears it.

UpdateTableClassificationBody.description: Request to update a table classification.

UpdateTicketStatusRequest.description:
The explicit transitions a tenant may drive: resolve, close, or reopen.
`pending_support`/`pending_customer` are derived from the conversation and
are rejected here.

skill_registries.description:
The complete new list — this is a replace, not a merge, so an empty list
detaches everything. Capped at
`MAX_SKILL_REGISTRIES_PER_WORKSTATION`.

UpdateWorkstationTemplateRequest.description:
Request body for updating an existing workstation template.
All fields are optional: absent fields leave the existing value unchanged.

script.description:
Send an empty string `""` to clear the explicit script and fall back to
the tooling-generated one. Absent = do not change the script.

tooling.description:
Replaces the tooling list. When provided (with no `script`), triggers
script regeneration from the new tooling.

UsageSource.description:
Which store backs a consumption read.

`Realtime` computes the window live from VictoriaMetrics (`increase()` over
the gateway counters — fresh to the last scrape, bounded by vmsingle's 30d
retention). `History` reads the durable Postgres rollup (≤1h latency,
survives TSDB eviction) — the accounting source the PDF report is pinned to.

UsageSummary.description: Aggregate token totals for a query window.

UserAttributesEntry.description: Entry for a single user's attributes.

attribute_sources.description: Maps attribute names to the provider name that supplied them.

UserDenialCount.description: Count of denials for a user.

ValueFormat.description: How a numeric cell is displayed (issue #2959).

VettedBaseResponse.description: A single base image the picker may offer: vetted and not retired.

VulnerabilityCounts.description:
Per-severity finding counts for one scanned digest. v1 is informational only
(the blocking quality gate is a v2.x follow-up).

WarningSeverity.description:
Severity shapes the UI's visual treatment: `danger` is red (Argo/Flux
resurrection), `warning` is amber (pipeline resurrection, cascading
drops), `info` is blue (child counts, row estimates).

WidgetHealth.description: Per-widget result of a dashboard health check (issue #2961).

error.description: The Trino validation error when `ok` is false.

WidgetLayout.description: Position and size on the dashboard's 12-column grid.

WorkstationFile.description:
One repo file surfaced by the read-only file finder. `path` is repo-relative
(the shape opencode's `/find/file` returns); `name` is the basename, derived
here so the frontend doesn't have to split paths.

name.description: Basename, e.g. `main.rs`.

WorkstationRepositoryInput.description:
A repository to clone into a workstation. Used both at create time (for the
additional repositories) and by the add-a-repository endpoint.

provider.description:
SCM provider: `github`, `gitlab` or `forgejo`. Must match the
workstation's primary provider — the in-pod git credential helper is
host-blind, so a single token has to work for every repository. With
`gitlab` that means the same instance too, self-managed or not.

repo_ref.description: Branch/tag to check out. Defaults to `main`.

WorkstationRepositoryResponse.description: One repository of a workstation, as the console shows it.

dir.description:
Directory the repo is cloned into, relative to `/workspace`. This is the
value to pass as the `repo` parameter on the git and file endpoints.

id.description:
`null` for the primary repository: it has no row of its own and cannot be
removed (it is the workstation's identity, fixed at create time).

WorkstationSkillRegistriesResponse.description: A workstation's attached registries, as read back from its CR.

WorkstationTemplateResponse.description: A workstation template as returned by the API.

baseImage.description: Base image the workstation pod will run on.

name.description: Kubernetes CRD name — the stable identifier for subsequent API calls.

setupScript.description:
The resolved setup script that the operator runs at provisioning.
